The trained model also outperforms Nemotron 3 Super, post-trained from the same base model, across all evaluations when comparing each model's best tested configuration. On EdgeBench, organisations overtake the single agent after approximately 0.4 derived hours. Over the course of training, organisations develop hierarchies to manage communication costs, invest more in peer review, and alter how work is divided. Safety evaluations find near-universal refusal of harmful actions but sustained declines in external reporting in two of three oversight scenarios. These results establish a shared-advantage baseline for studying organisational learning, performance-latency trade-offs, and collective oversight.

candidates.title: EmbodiedStudio: A Task-Driven Simulation Generation Platform for Embodied Learning and Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Training and evaluating robots across diverse tasks requires a supply of simulation environments suited to those tasks. While recent scene and task generators offer a promising way to expand this supply, delivering a usable task environment still faces two practical gaps: generated scenes that look plausible in appearance often fail to support the intended task interactions or remain physically stable in simulation, and generated scoring programs frequently attempt task conditions without implementing them faithfully. We present EmbodiedStudio, a task-driven simulation generation platform that bridges these gaps by jointly authoring scene, task, robot-behavior, and rubric programs under closed-loop simulation feedback and independent review. Crucially, as the coding agent iteratively debugs scenes, behaviors, and stateful rubrics in simulation, this closed-loop process natively yields both forward construction experience for learning to build environments and physical execution experience for policy learning, all bound to frozen environment revisions for repeatable evaluation. Across scene generation, rubric evaluation, ablations, and learning studies, EmbodiedStudio substantially improves task readiness and rubric faithfulness while improving physical stability and retaining actionable supervision signals for layout authoring and policy adaptation.

candidates.title: Next-Manip: On-Demand Agent-Policy Collaboration for Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: General-purpose robotic manipulation requires task reasoning, failure recovery, and precise control, yet limited manipulation data make these abilities difficult to obtain from a single policy. Recent multimodal agents show promise in task reasoning and recovery but lack reliable fine-grained control and incur high inference cost, whereas learned policies provide efficient fine-grained execution but struggle beyond their learned skills. Although their complementary strengths suggest combining the two, doing so requires repeatedly deciding which executor should act as task demands change. Instead of relying on the agent for each decision, we present Next-Manip, an on-demand agent--policy collaboration framework that decouples executor allocation from costly agent inference. We propose an Agent Invocation Controller (AIC) that allocates control between the policy and the agent through a lightweight classifier of current execution demands. We further introduce Task Dynamics Context (TDC), which packages informative manipulation changes from in-context examples into compact task references to support both agent reasoning and executor allocation. Across two simulation benchmarks and real-world experiments, Next-Manip achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing agent inference costs.

candidates.title: ContinualDrive: A Deployment-Anchored, Multi-Axis Benchmark for Continual Updates of Learned Driving Planners
candidates.abstract: Learned driving planners keep being updated after deployment as new logs arrive, yet continual learning evaluations rarely ask whether an update improves on the deployed model, and their verdicts rest on unstated evaluation choices. We present ContinualDrive, a deployment-anchored benchmark for post-deployment continual learning of driving planners. It updates a deployed planner on real-world nuPlan logs one scenario-type group at a time, evaluates the same checkpoints in open and closed loop, makes four measurement axes explicit (evaluation loop, reference checkpoint, temporal aggregation and stream protocol), and anchors a three-valued release verdict to the deployed checkpoint. We study two planners (PlanTF and Diffusion Planner) under full fine-tuning and adapter or LoRA updates, with and without replay or gradient projection, in three task orders. Verdicts can reverse or vanish when one axis changes: open-loop ADE ranks the final PlanTF model above the deployed one in half of its core-suite runs, whereas every closed-loop score ranks it below; backward transfer misses this loss, which on average is already present when each group has just been learned; and regime rankings vary far less across training seeds than across task orders. In the core suite of full and adapter updates, no regime measurably improved on the deployed planner in closed loop; on a panel more than ten times larger every evaluated final checkpoint trails it, and joint training on all groups recovers much of the loss without exceeding its nuPlan closed-loop score. We distill these findings into a reporting contract and will release the code and all checkpoints.
candidates.comment: 34 pages (8 main pages + references + 22-page supplement), 4 figures in the main text. Code: https://github.com/continualdrive/benchmark . Project page: https://lzrbit.github.io/continualdrive/

candidates.title: What If Chinese Were Latinized? A Counterfactual Study of Input Representation, Tokenization, and Language Modeling
candidates.abstract: If Chinese had been Latinized, as the Latinxua Sin Wenz movement proposed, what would it have meant for Chinese NLP? Homophones and tone marking complicate the answer. We convert Chinese corpora to syllable-separated Pinyin and train superBPE tokenizers from scratch. The resulting Pinyin vocabularies not only exhibit expected homophone collisions, but also show approximately 10% higher fertility than characters. An alternative BPE configuration changes the relative fertility of the two representations. We further pretrain Llama-style models on Chinese characters and Pinyin. The Pinyin models perform worse on per-character perplexity, homophone disambiguation, and overall ZhoBLiMP minimal-pair accuracy. An exploratory phonological probe yields near-chance performance for both representations. The broader implication is that written input representations are not merely neutral encodings. Choices for representations affect language modeling and their downstream performances. Latinization never actually happened for Chinese, but other languages did, such as Hangul and Latin script replaced character in Korean and Vietnamese; the cost we measure is a guide to where modeling effort for those languages should concentrate.

candidates.title: AirLeg: A Robust and Accurate Self-Supervised Visual-Inertial-Leg SLAM System
candidates.abstract: Visual-inertial-leg (VIL) state estimation offers cost-effective localization for legged robots, adding only a camera to the onboard IMU and joint encoders. However, learning-based leg odometry is limited by its supervision: networks trained in simulation suffer from the sim-to-real gap, while real-world labels require costly sensors or inherit the errors of visual estimates. To address this, we present AirLeg, a self-supervised VIL SLAM system in which vision and leg proprioception improve each other from training to deployment. We pre-train the leg odometry network in simulation and adapt it to the robot without ground truth through imperative learning, where multi-sensor bundle adjustment uses the leg odometry to refine the visual map, which in turn supervises the network. During deployment, the fused estimates adapt the network online. To improve both localization and this supervision, a dual-window estimator fuses vision, IMU, and leg odometry, relates loaded feet to the visually reconstructed terrain through a deformation-aware constraint, and weights the constraints by variance component estimation. AirLeg completes all 17 GrandTour sequences with the lowest average error (0.19 m) among 19 methods. On a low-cost quadruped, it achieves the lowest drift (0.6%) with only 0.5 h of unlabeled data, in real time on an embedded computer.

candidates.title: Branch and Consolidate: A Unified Recipe for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
candidates.abstract: Specialists post-trained from a shared checkpoint acquire complementary capabilities, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) can consolidate them into a single model. However, we find that existing consolidation methods, from weight merging to MOPD, fall short when specialists diverge substantially from the shared checkpoint, whereas prior studies mostly examine specialists that remain close to it. We present a unified recipe for multimodal MOPD that consolidates such specialists back into the single student they branched from. The recipe specifies initialization, data selection, balanced supervision across teachers, and preservation of existing capabilities for consolidation, together with a targeted refinement stage for capabilities that still lag behind their specialists. In an industrial setting with six specialists, the student closely approaches each specialist in its own domain and surpasses the perception specialist. It recovers 97.0% of their average gain, compared with 79.8% for IM-MOPD. In the fully open five-domain setting with Qwen3-4B, our method recovers 95.7% of the specialists' average gain after consolidation and 97.5% after refinement, compared with 94.1% for IM-MOPD. We further analyze the full pipeline through mechanism ablations and training dynamics, providing practical guidance for diagnosing incomplete consolidation. Code will be released.

candidates.title: RecurSciBench: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement in Data-Driven Scientific Research
candidates.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are advancing the automation of data-driven scientific research. Recent advances in recursive self-improvement (RSI) offer the potential for these agents to continuously improve through experience, but evaluating transfer across scientific tasks requires executable, scientifically verifiable tasks and independent assessment of self-improvement gains. We introduce RecurSciBench, a scalable benchmark for evaluating RSI in data-driven scientific research. Its RecurSciPipe framework automatically constructs scientific modeling and data analysis tasks from raw datasets, with execution-based verification and scientific validity checks. RecurSciBench spans four scientific domains, multiple data modalities, and varied scientific objectives. We evaluate four RSI systems by comparing their initial and evolved states on independent tasks after evolution on source tasks, covering within-type, cross-type, and cross-domain transfer. Experiments show that the benefits of self-improvement vary across agent systems and scientific domains. Positive overall gains can coexist with regressions on individual tasks. Experience can transfer across task types and benefit other domains even without measurable gains in the source domain.

candidates.title: InducedTFMs: A Family of Sub-Quadratic Tabular Foundation Models Using Induced Attention
candidates.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) have emerged as a serious competitor to gradient-boosted trees, predicting on a new table in a single forward pass by in-context learning. However, their attention is quadratic in the number of samples and features, which caps pretraining at small synthetic tables and forces inference on large ones to rely on chunking or subsampling. Row-compression models reduce the feature-wise cost, but only by discarding the cell-level representation, and remain quadratic in the number of samples. We introduce InducedTFM, which replaces both attention stages of a bidimensional TFM with the induced attention of the Set Transformer, preserving cell-level representations while making its cost linear in both samples and features. Under a training budget matched to a full-attention TabICLv2 reimplementation, InducedTFM matches its accuracy on TabArena and on a benchmark of larger datasets, and clearly outperforms a kernel linear-attention baseline of the same asymptotic cost. It overtakes TabICLv2 in inference time on narrow tables, reaching a 30x speed-up at 640K rows, although row compression remains preferable on wide tables.

candidates.title: MRCT: An Object-Centric Two-Layer Control Architecture for Heavy-Payload Multi-Robot Transportation
candidates.abstract: Cooperative transportation of heavy payloads by heterogeneous mobile manipulators requires coordinated payload motion, force distribution, and compliant physical interaction. This paper presents MRCT, an object-centric two-layer control architecture for multi-robot transportation. At the object level, a model predictive controller (MPC) generates a coordinated contact-force reference for the payload. At the robot level, whole- body impedance control (WBIC) modules on individual robots realise the reference through a confidence-based blending of velocity-tracking and impedance torques. The blending mechanism emphasises tracking when the joint-velocity error is small and increases compliance when tracking degrades because of abrupt reference changes or physical disturbances. Simulation and hardware experiments with a heterogeneous team comprising a single-arm and a dual-arm mobile manipulator transporting a near-rated table payload demonstrate accurate object tracking, regulated contact forces, and stable payload orientation. Parameter sensitivity studies, obstacle-avoidance transportation, and step-load disturbance experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of MRCT for reliable cooperative transportation under the evaluated conditions

candidates.title: Assessing Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cyber-Physical Systems
candidates.abstract: As the use of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes more widespread in cyber-physical systems, it becomes increasingly important to design RL agents that are able to adapt to changes in their environments in order to maintain safety and reliability. This paper addresses the question of whether different classes of RL algorithm are more robust against forgetting previously learned behaviours, a critical issue in continual learning, in non-stationary environments. We evaluate the robustness of representative examples of three important classes of RL algorithm in a non-stationary autonomous parking environment. These are Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which is a model-free on-policy algorithm, Soft-Actor-Critic (SAC), which is a model-free off-policy algorithm, and Drama, which is a model-based algorithm. The agents must learn to successfully park in four different scenarios, which are presented successively, with parking spaces oriented at varying angles. We find off-policy algorithms appear to be more robust compared to on-policy algorithms due to their use of replay, while model-based algorithms do not appear to offer any direct advantage over model-free algorithms. These experiments also highlight the additional challenges of finding robust abstractions of the environment, and oversensitivity to hyperparameters.
candidates.comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, 1 table, Accepted to SGAI 2026. This preprint has not undergone peer review or any post-submission improvements or corrections. The Version of Record is published in 'Artificial Intelligence XLIII' and is available online at https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-45236-8_34

candidates.title: CoFiNav: VLM-Guided Coarse-to-Fine Semantic Navigation for Open-Ended Last-Mile UAV Delivery
candidates.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) delivery is an important application of the low-altitude economy, enhancing the flexibility and accessibility of last-mile logistics. Existing UAV delivery methods generally rely on precise terminal coordinates, predefined terminal specifications, or task-specific localization procedures, limiting the scope and flexibility of delivery. As UAV logistics becomes more intelligent, open-ended semantic descriptions offer a new paradigm for specifying terminal destinations. However, conventional aerial navigation methods have limited ability to generalize to delivery scenarios that require open-vocabulary terminal navigation. To enable this broader delivery paradigm, we propose CoFiNav, a VLM-guided coarse-to-fine UAV semantic navigation framework that progressively grounds relation-defined terminal destinations through hierarchical semantic search and active 3D observation. Given a task description, a coarse prior map from OpenStreetMap (OSM), and accumulated observations, CoFiNav uses a vision-language model (VLM) to determine which unresolved entity or spatial relation should be verified next. A geometry-aware module converts the semantic observation request into feasible viewpoints using RGB images and LiDAR, while conventional motion planning handles safe execution. Experiments across multiple urban environments show that CoFiNav outperforms representative adapted baselines in success rate while requiring shorter flight paths and fewer observations.

candidates.title: When Knowledge-Tracing Rankings Depend on Available History: A Source-Correction and Matched-Information Audit on ASSISTments 2009 and 2015
candidates.abstract: Knowledge-tracing benchmarks often compare models that have different access to a learner's previous responses. We examine how data provenance, history length, and representation affect those comparisons. First, we compare a pinned ASSISTments 2009 sequence mirror against the corrected official release. Of 4,148 learners represented in both, 817 have different ordered skill-response sequences; the mirror also contains fewer labeled events. Second, we retain earlier learner-disjoint model evaluations on the 2009 and 2015 datasets, distinguishing exploratory results from a corrective 2015 replication. Finally, we evaluate a new, nonoverlapping sample of 4,000 ASSISTments 2015 learners using three models constrained to the same one-event or 20-event prior-response window. On 20,592 test responses from 582 learners, the 20-event Brier scores were 0.17667 for count-based logistic regression, 0.17389 for an order-aware logistic model, and 0.17514 for a GRU. The GRU-minus-order-aware difference was 0.00125 (95% learner-cluster bootstrap interval [0.00008, 0.00243]); at one prior event, the corresponding difference was 0.00212 [0.00120, 0.00301]. Earlier comparisons had favored the GRU against simpler history summaries. The newer analysis instead favors a logistic comparator that represents order using the same permitted event stream. These results concern predictive performance on particular historical cohorts and model settings. They neither isolate an architectural effect nor establish generalization to contemporary classrooms.

candidates.title: CodeWAM: A Code World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
candidates.abstract: Driving world models anticipate action consequences through representations of how the world evolves. For autonomous driving, these representations must capture both the surrounding scene and the ego vehicle's motion under a candidate plan. We propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that incorporates executable code as part of its world representation. Code represents ego dynamics by expressing how the vehicle state evolves under plan execution, while a learned visual model captures scene-dependent consequences. Executing the code produces a candidate-conditioned motion sequence, which is evaluated relative to the prior plan and recorded motion history. The resulting execution consequences and learned scene outcomes jointly represent the candidate's future, enabling the planner to assess both what a plan may lead to and how the vehicle transitions into that future. The selected plan becomes part of the next decision's execution context, linking successive choices within the model. CodeWAM achieves 93.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, 92.1 EPDMS on v2 navtest, and 50.6 EPDMS on NAVHARD. Further experiments demonstrate improved pairwise execution consistency and gains on Hydra-MDP and DrivoR without additional training, supporting executable code as a complementary representation for driving world models.

candidates.title: VISE: Verifier-Independent Skill Self-Evolution with Feedback from Tool Implementations
candidates.abstract: Agent skills provide reusable workflows that guide LLM agents in using tools. Refining these workflows requires feedback on missing or incorrect instructions, but task-specific verifiers are not always available. We propose VISE (Verifier-Independent Skill Evolution), a scripts-first approach that uses tool implementations to guide skill revision. It extracts tool capabilities, input requirements, usage conditions, and output formats from source code. Using the task request and execution trace, it compares this information with current workflow instructions to identify missing or conflicting steps. It then recommends specific edits to SKILL.md, linking each change to the relevant implementation and usage conditions. We evaluate VISE as an additional revision stage for four evolution methods on SkillsBench and SkillLearnBench. Compared with the corresponding No-verifier conditions, it improves overall average task success by 9.14-13.35 percentage points. The proportion of tasks solved in all three runs increases by 12.36-18.29 points. A case study shows how revised instructions connect tool outputs to later steps. These results support tool implementations as a practical feedback source for skill self-evolution.

candidates.title: ViTacLab: Physically Consistent Visuo-Tactile Simulation, Benchmarking, and Representation Learning for Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Tactile sensing is essential for contact-rich robotic manipulation, but existing visuo-tactile simulators trade physical fidelity for scalability, and benchmarks largely focus on two-finger grippers. We present ViTacLab, a framework comprising ViTacSim, ViTacBench, and ViTacPolicy. ViTacSim uses a tri-modal tactile primitive: a global sparse contact-force lattice, a local dense force array, and tactile images. Anchored to PhysX contact-solver outputs, it corrects normal inconsistency through local stiffness alignment and reconstructs tangential forces under decoupled slip-stick regimes while preserving GPU parallelism. A joint projection preserves the sparse wrench and enforces local friction cones. ViTacBench spans parallel grippers, dexterous hands, and bimanual systems, with tasks ranging from vision-dominant to tactile-dominant regimes. ViTacPolicy aggregates variable numbers of heterogeneous tactile inputs using spatial-pose embeddings and a Transformer, and aligns force-array and tactile-image modalities through a two-stream VQ-VAE with a shared codebook. Controlled Hertzian-reference indentation and real-sensor sliding tests reduce normal and tangential force RMSE from 2.31 and 1.85 N to 0.42 and 0.53 N, respectively. Throughput reaches 2,482.9 tactile-pipeline FPS at 256 parallel environments. Simulation and real-world experiments show gains on several contact-rich tasks, while low absolute success on tactile-dominant tasks highlights the remaining difficulty of purely tactile control.

candidates.title: ROVO: Robust Rotation-Only Visual Odometry for UAVs at Low and Moderate Altitudes
candidates.abstract: Image noise can confound rotation and translation estimates in monocular visual navigation for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) at low and moderate altitudes, where even small perturbations may cause large errors in translation direction. Inspired by angular cues in long-range visual perception, we propose rotation-only visual odometry (ROVO) for monocular aerial imagery. ROVO estimates pairwise rotations from matched images, robustly averages them over overlapping windows, and aligns consecutive windows through shared frames. By retaining only orientation in the trajectory state, it prevents uncertain landmark depth from propagating to later estimates. In trajectory simulation, sliding-window ROVO achieved a mean orientation error just 10.7% as large as that of the conventional SLAM baseline. On real flight data, ROVO achieved rotation accuracy comparable to ORB-SLAM3 and DPVO under the original Bell412 settings. With a narrower FoV or at higher flight altitude, ROVO reduced relative rotation RMSE by 19.7--69.4% compared with the next-best method in each comparison. Code and simulation tools are available at https://github.com/sssxxxkkkk/ROVO.

candidates.title: BCP: A Lightweight Boundary-Controlled Framework for Online Sign Language Recognition and Translation
candidates.abstract: Online sign language recognition (SLR) and translation (SLT) incrementally produce gloss sequences or natural language text from sign video as it arrives, a capability essential for real-time communication and live captioning. However, powerful pretrained offline models cannot be directly deployed in this setting, while existing online methods typically retrain the entire model on simulated streaming prefixes constructed from offline videos, incurring high costs. To address this challenge, we propose Boundary-Controlled Prefix Commit (BCP), a unified lightweight framework that converts pretrained offline methods into online counterparts for sign-to-gloss (S2G), sign-to-text (S2T), and sign-to-gloss-to-text (S2G2T). Specifically, BCP freezes the pretrained model and introduces a lightweight boundary adapter that decides when to commit, supervised by Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) alignments from a pretrained SLR model, without any human annotation. At inference, a Boundary-Controlled Wait-K Output Policy then decides what to commit via prefix voting, yielding adaptive burst commits while preserving the output progress of the base Wait-K schedule. Experiments on PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily across four offline methods show that BCP, with less than 0.1% additional trainable parameters per offline method, achieves a strong quality-latency trade-off on S2T and remains competitive on S2G and S2G2T.

candidates.title: Phoneme-identity depth profiles do not reliably predict LoRA placement for dysarthric ASR
candidates.abstract: Parameter-efficient adaptation of a speech foundation model to dysarthric speech requires a rarely justified choice: which encoder layers to adapt. A recently proposed strategy is to probe the encoder, find where phonetic information becomes most decodable, and put the adapters there. We test that inference across two ASR models (Qwen3-ASR, Whisper-small) and two dysarthric corpora (Mandarin CDSD, English UASpeech), holding recipe and seed discipline constant. The inference fails. Measured under one pipeline rather than inherited from published figures, all four phoneme-error curves minimise between 83% and 92% of relative depth, each model's minimising layer moving no further between corpora than between probe seeds. The best adaptation band is not similarly constant: none of three natural mappings from the curve to a band -- steepest improvement, lowest band-mean error, or knee location -- recovers the best tested configuration. We do not claim no statistic of the curve could work, only that these three do not. Placement still matters, but is model- and corpus-specific. On CDSD the models disagree -- Qwen3-ASR prefers its upper third (29.88% CER, three-seed mean), Whisper-small all-block LoRA (53.56%) -- while on UASpeech neither favours the upper band. At three seeds, upper-versus-all is resolved (-1.31 pp, CI [-2.16, -0.25]) but upper-versus-middle is not (-0.83 pp, CI [-2.06, +1.86]). The two models' preferences differ as a directly tested interaction (-4.71 pp, CI [-6.17, -2.89]); we designate this the primary claim, and record that the designation was made post hoc. On Qwen3-ASR x UASpeech, adapting near the input is reliably worse than not adapting at all (+9.90 pp CER). We recommend choosing the band by a short adaptation sweep on the model and corpus in hand, not by reading it off a probe.

candidates.title: The Teacher Is Already Inside: Self-Distilling Looped Language Models Beyond Their Last Loop
candidates.abstract: Looped language models apply one shared transformer stack several times per token, and every loop is readable through the shared language-model head. Post-training them is hard. Reward-only reinforcement learning needs a verifier and learns from one sparse signal per response; spreading the reward over loops collapses the entropy of every loop; and cross-loop self-distillation, as in LoopOPD, can only teach intermediate loops, because the last loop cannot learn from its own frozen copy: the loss is zero at initialisation. We observe that a looped model already contains a policy that decodes better than its last loop: the next-token distribution extrapolated from the first loop through the last. ELPSD (Extrapolated-Loop Policy Self-Distillation) turns this distribution into a self-distillation target: a frozen copy of the model computes it, and the model's own last loop is distilled towards it on its own rollouts, using the exact reverse KL at every visited prefix. Teacher and student are the same model, so ELPSD needs no reward, no external teacher and no privileged context, and it leaves rollouts and decoding unchanged. We show that the objective pulls the last loop towards the base model's last loop with weight 1+w and away from the base model's first loop with weight w, and that the teacher must stay frozen, since an idealised teacher recomputed from the current model extrapolates without bound. We evaluate ELPSD on Ouro-1.4B-Thinking across five math benchmarks against the base model, GRPO, RLTT and OPSD. Without any reward, ELPSD raises the average avg@8 from 61.15 to 63.69 and is the best method on all five benchmarks, ahead of GRPO (62.32), which uses a verifier, and the self-distillation method OPSD (61.77), which needs reference solutions.

candidates.title: When Ink Meets Pixel: Intent-Aware OCR with VLMs for Human-Corrected Financial Documents When Ink Meets Pixel: Intent-Aware OCR with VLMs for Human-Corrected Financial Documents
candidates.abstract: Human annotations on documents (such as arrows, carets, strikethroughs, and insertions) express corrective intent yet existing OCR and document understanding systems treat these marks as visual noise rather than semantic edit operations. We introduce intent-aware OCR, the task of generating corrected transcriptions by jointly reasoning over original document content and visual intent cues (handwritten or digital) that convey edit intent. To support this setting, we present DocIntent, a multimodal dataset of 1,600 financial documents with over 5,700 annotated visual intent cues, each paired with layout-aware, intent-resolved OCR targets. We further introduce IntentBench, a 216-document benchmark designed to evaluate model robustness under diverse real-world annotation conditions. Leveraging DocIntent, we fine-tune DocIntentOCR, a suite of 3B and 7B parameter vision-language models, under direct intent supervision on corrected transcriptions. On IntentBench, the fine-tuned 3B and 7B models achieve F1-scores of 0.81 and 0.83, respectively, substantially outperforming commercial closed-source (e.g., GPT-4.1 (0.626)), and open-source models (e.g., LLaMA-3.2-Vision-90B (0.50)) demonstrating that intent-aware supervision enables compact domain-specific models to outperform substantially larger general-purpose systems on this task. This work establishes intent-aware OCR as a novel human-in-the-loop document understanding task and provides foundational resources (dataset, benchmark, models) to advance research in interactive document processing.

candidates.title: See the Answer, Learn to Embed: Learning Universal Multimodal Embeddings from Hindsight
candidates.abstract: Universal Multimodal Embedding (UME) models map heterogeneous multimodal inputs into a shared embedding space, where pairwise similarity supports diverse downstream tasks. Recent reasoning-driven UME approaches use intermediate reasoning to generate additional context for embedding, but often incur extra computation at inference. In this paper, we explore the matched candidate (i.e., the paired target) as an alternative source of context, asking whether a model can "see the answer" during training and "learn to embed" without it at inference. However, direct conditioning on this privileged context can introduce candidate-specific information unavailable from the query alone or cause the candidate-conditioned query representation to collapse toward the candidate embedding. To address this, we introduce Hindsight-Enhanced Multimodal Embeddings (HEME), which learns query-grounded hindsight representations from such candidate context. HEME first trains a hindsight teacher with a hindsight attention mask, mismatched-candidate conditioning, and query-token alignment to limit excessive reliance on the candidate. It then freezes the teacher and distills its hindsight representation and similarity distribution into a standalone student embedder. At inference, the student independently encodes queries and candidates without candidate conditioning or the hindsight teacher. Experiments on MMEB-V2 and the agent and text tasks of MMEB-V3 demonstrate the effectiveness of HEME and show that it enables more efficient inference than explicit reasoning-driven methods.

candidates.title: On the Importance of Hidden-State Refinement in Masked Diffusion Language Models
candidates.abstract: Masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising masked or corrupted token sequences, allowing token predictions to condition on bidirectional context and update multiple positions in parallel. While each denoising step produces a rich layer-wise hidden-state trajectory, prior work typically focuses only on token-level information and discards these continuous hidden states, leaving their refinement dynamics underexplored. In this work, we analyze hidden-state dynamics in MDLMs and find clear evidence of layer-wise and cross-step refinement: smooth evolution across adjacent layers, greater predictive power in deeper layers, gradual degradation under transformer block removal, and strong final-state alignment across consecutive denoising steps. Motivated by these observations, we propose Cross-Step Recurrent Refinement (CSRR), a mechanism that carries hidden-state information across denoising steps to enhance generation. Extensive experiments show that CSRR improves text generation quality, highlighting the critical role of continuous hidden-state refinement in MDLMs. Project page: https://zhongzero.github.io/Recurrent-DLLM/

candidates.title: A Face Robot which Imitates Human Musculoskeletal Skin System and Its Evaluation on Basic Movement of Facial Expression
candidates.abstract: Facial robots require many coordinated, smallamplitude motions, but accommodating these motions in a compact face remains difficult. This paper presents an anatomically inspired facial-robot platform that reproduces the layered organization of the human facial musculoskeletal system. The platform comprises bone, muscle, and skin components whose geometry, shape, and attachment locations are derived from three-dimensional anatomical data. Wire-driven, compliant muscle components are routed through PTFE tubes, allowing actuation to be placed away from the face. We describe the selection and fabrication of 65 muscles (34 muscle types) required to reproduce the 47 target action units (AUs) in the Facial Action Coding System (FACS). We then evaluate the reproducibility of individual AUs in two stages: muscle actuation without skin and actuation after the silicone skin is attached. Forty of the 47 target AUs were reproduced with the muscle components, and 30 were reproduced after skin attachment. These results demonstrate the feasibility of reproducing a broad range of FACS facial expressions using an anatomically inspired musculoskeletal structure. The proposed platform provides a foundation for the systematic development and evaluation of future anatomically inspired facial robots
candidates.comment: Accepted to IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2026, website - https://haraduka.github.io/musculoskeletal-face/, youtube - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eRuoUJ056uc

candidates.title: Delay-Tolerant Formation Tracking for Multi-AGV Systems via Reference-Shift Coupling
candidates.abstract: Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) that transport a load together must keep a formation while each vehicle tracks its own reference, and they coordinate over wireless links with link-dependent, time-varying and jumping delays. We propose a cascade design for differential-drive AGVs modelled as kinematic unicycles: delayed data from the neighbours drive only a second-order filter that shifts each vehicle's own reference, and an unmodified gain-scheduled tracking law follows the shifted reference. A saturation keeps the shifted reference feasible, and the feed-forward is exact, so the tracking loop never sees the network. We prove that tracking and formation errors remain bounded for arbitrary delays and converge for every bounded delay and every directed, possibly switching, graph. We also construct a strict Lyapunov function with explicit constants and prove exponential convergence and a local input-to-state estimate with delay-independent gains. On undirected graphs, the coupling attenuates the formation error caused by persistent local errors by at least the factor lambda/(lambda+Lambda*lambda_2(L)) (leak lambda, coupling gain Lambda, algebraic connectivity lambda_2(L)), for any delay. Every inequality is verified with an event-driven, error-controlled simulation. A robustness study on a high-fidelity AGV model (drive dynamics, slip, localisation errors, clock offsets, lossy Wi-Fi) comprises 4,894 runs, including paired comparisons against tuned baselines. The cascade never failed, with latencies up to 4 s, 90% packet loss and up to 12 vehicles, whereas a direct delayed coupling failed when its gain saturated the drives. Coupling reduced the formation error after traction losses by 21-32% and after safety stops by up to 47%, at the price of tracking accuracy. Localisation bias and clock offsets, which no coupling law can observe, limit the achievable accuracy.

candidates.title: A Framework for Graph Node Symmetric Quantification under Dataset Shift
candidates.abstract: Graph node quantification is the supervised learning task of estimating the prevalence of different classes within an arbitrary sample of unlabelled nodes from a graph, subject to some form of dataset shift. Existing approaches to graph node quantification typically follow the standard aggregative paradigm, i.e., they use labelled nodes from the graph to train an intermediate node classifier, and obtain an estimated class distribution for the sample by aggregating the classifier's predictions for the individual nodes and then correcting the result via some adjustment strategy that accounts for dataset shift. In this work we propose a framework for graph node quantification that does away with both node-level supervision, since its training phase only requires node samples labelled by their class distribution, and node-level predictions, since it estimates class prevalence values directly, without the need of any intermediate node classifier. The framework thus allows symmetric quantification, since (unlike in standard ``asymmetric'' quantification methods) the labelled items used for training and the unlabelled items on which predictions must be issued are of the same type (i.e., node samples). This framework (that we dub GSQ, for Graph Node Symmetric Quantification) allows building pipelines consisting of a node encoder, an embedding pooler, a prevalence predictor, and an optional post-hoc scaling step. These components can be instantiated by choosing from different trainable and reservoir-based encoders, different pooling operators, and different prediction objectives. We evaluate the GSQ framework on binary and multi-class datasets with different levels of homophily, under prior probability shift and under structural covariate shift.

candidates.title: Optimal Transport Meets t-SNE: Integrated Visualization without Batch Effects in OT-tSNE
candidates.abstract: Visual exploration is an integral step in understanding the structure of datasets. However, systematic variation between datasets collected under different conditions, known as batch effects, can obscure shared structure and complicate their joint visualization. Existing methods often rely on cross-batch nearest-neighbor relations to integrate the batches. Yet, these local correspondences can be unreliable for challenging cross-batch geometries. We propose optimal-transport t-SNE (OT-tSNE), which replaces nearest-neighbor-based matching with globally coupled affinities derived from entropic optimal transport. Controlled synthetic experiments demonstrated that nearest-neighbor-based methods can deteriorate, while optimal-transport affinities and OT-tSNE embeddings remain robust. Across seven real single-cell datasets, we benchmarked OT-tSNE against a broad range of integration and visualization methods and found that it achieves a Pareto-efficient trade-off between batch mixing and biological conservation, and integrates batches particularly well.
candidates.comment: 35 pages, 18 figures, 5 tables. Code at https://github.com/NDR-lab/ot-tsne

candidates.title: Not All Pairs Align: Caption-Guided Audio-Visual Contrastive Learning
candidates.abstract: We address the problem of learning audio-visual representations from co-occurring modalities. Multimodal contrastive learning typically assumes that paired observations provide shared views of the same underlying information. While this may be true for datasets collected in constrained environments, it does not always hold. For instance, co-occurring audio and visual signals can differ substantially in their content due to off-screen sounds. Nevertheless, standard contrastive objectives treat all paired samples as equally aligned. In this work, we propose Caption Guided Alignment Aware Loss (CGAAL), a model-agnostic objective that leverages modality-specific captions to estimate semantic agreement between audio and video. CGAAL uses these agreement scores to weight the contribution of each positive pair. A warm-up period and gradual thresholding strategy progressively introduce this alignment-aware training signal. We demonstrate the generality of CGAAL by applying it to three contrastive baselines, consistently improving their performance on audio-visual retrieval.

candidates.title: Fractal Neural Synthesis: Constant-Storage Procedural Weight Derivation via Complex Quadratic Boundary Dynamics
candidates.abstract: Conventional neural networks store synaptic parameters as explicit tensors whose persistent Flash footprint scales linearly (O(W)) with parameter count, constraining resource-limited edge microcontrollers. We formulate and systematically evaluate Fractal Neural Synthesis (FNS), a procedural weight derivation architecture that replaces hidden-layer matrices with a constant 24-byte coordinate seed Theta = (c_x, c_y, ell) in F_64^3 anchored near the complex quadratic bifurcation boundary dM of f_c(z) = z^2 + c. We introduce a large-bailout (R = 256) smooth escape kernel, four zero-overhead geometric sampling apertures--Cartesian Grid, coprime 3x3 Rule-of-Thirds (Z/9Z), phi-Vogel spiral, and multi-scale Harmonic Tripod--and prove conditional Kolmogorov (K_Kolm <= 192 + c_0 bits) and Shannon entropy bounds. Across magnifications zeta in [10^0, 10^8], C^1 Fourier and lattice-noise bases collapse to post-standardization rank ~2.25 and SHA-256 PRNG exhibits avalanche discontinuity (rho ~ 0.019, 50.6% micro-step retention), whereas dM uniquely sustains both rank (~10.0) and local continuity (rho in [0.81, 0.97], 89.2% retention). Under leak-free 10-fold CV across four zero-scaler-byte non-linear benchmarks, FNS with an INT8 readout surpasses 0-hidden Linear-INT8 by +3.6 to +10.8 pp while delivering 10.7x-129x total Flash reduction (725x-2,773x hidden reduction) relative to converged Float32 MLPs (90.30% Ionosphere in 285 B; 97.22% Optical Digits in 2,598 B; 97.90% PenDigits in 2,598 B; 87.00% Satimage in 1,570 B).
candidates.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Reproducible code, seeds, and raw benchmark telemetry archived under Zenodo Concept DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22774934

candidates.title: Evolve to Learn: Gradient-aligned experience evolution for model self-improvement
candidates.abstract: Self-evolving language models can continuously acquire useful experience through test-time interaction, reflection, and prompt optimization, yet turning such experience into model itself to ensure self improvement remains challenging. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) provides a natural mechanism for internalizing test-time information into model parameters, yet it largely assumes that the gener- ated experience is worth learning. We show that this assumption does not always hold: experiences that improve test-time performance may provide limited or even harmful training signals. To better characterize which experience should be inter- nalized, we systematically analyze diverse mutated experiences across multiple tasks and reflection models, and find that gradient-based alignment is a more reli- able indicator of downstream distillation gains than immediate test-time improve- ment. Based on this finding, we propose E2L, a self-evolution framework that iteratively generates, evaluates, and distills experiences according to their esti- mated training utility. E2L closes the loop between experience generation and parameter learning, enabling agents to autonomously produce experience suitable for self-improvement.

candidates.title: Can AI Design a Better nnU-Net? A Hypothesis-Driven Architecture Discovery Loop from Failures to Design Rules
candidates.abstract: Neural architecture search and LLM-driven evolution often reduce evaluation to a scalar fitness score, discarding failures that could explain why designs succeed or fail. We present a hypothesis-driven architecture discovery loop in which LLM agents diagnose structured error patterns, formulate falsifiable hypotheses, test counterfactual controls under a frozen nnU-Net pipeline, and distill validated mechanisms into executable trigger-to-action rules. Across eight search waves, the loop identifies two principles for 3D medical image segmentation. First, reallocating computation from high-resolution decoders to the mid-encoder preserves thin-anatomy boundaries while reducing cost. Second, support-confined region contrast addresses errors between nested anatomical compartments, with anatomy-dependent triggers selecting when the rule applies. These principles produce LeanNeXt (0.78 MACs and 0.92 training-step time relative to nnU-Net; +1.63 Dice points on four-fold KiTS23 cross-validation) and trigger-routed LeanNeXt+. The latter improves all 15 evaluated CT/MRI settings over nnU-Net and exceeds the 3.3 larger ResEnc-M on 12 of 15 benchmarks at 0.30 its parameter count. Relative to random sampling, one-shot LLM generation, and score-selected agent search, the loop shows how failure analysis can yield reusable design rules across modalities.

candidates.title: Does Research-Paper Context Improve LLM-Generated Quadruped Navigation? An Exploratory Simulation Study
candidates.abstract: Large language models can write competent robot navigation code, but not only does the research on the topic advance, a model may also, due to the volume of findings, fail to recall relevant findings and apply them to the task at hand. In this work, we test whether providing particular research papers as context improves the LLM-written navigation code for the Go2 quadruped, with the LLM (Claude Opus 5) and locomotion policy frozen. Specifically, we compare the navigation controllers the LLM writes when provided with and without particular papers across three settings: behavior trees, navigators edited from a shared base, and controllers written from scratch. When a maze's shortest route is blocked mid-episode, 2 of 8 controllers written with the context of an incremental-replanning paper complete all four trips under Isaac Sim physics, against 7 of 8 without it (two-sided Fisher's exact test, p = 0.041). This difference appears only under physics: in an idealized kinematic simulator, the controllers written with and without the paper are indistinguishable. We hypothesize that an LLM provided research papers as context tends to overweight both their content and their goals -- in this case, the efficiency of incremental replanning -- negatively affecting the fulfillment of the main task and leading to less robust code.

candidates.title: The Activity Geometry of Discrete Generative Sampling
candidates.abstract: Iterative refinement is a key capability of diffusion-based generation and has motivated growing efforts to bring similar behavior to discrete diffusion and flow models. A growing line of work enables such refinement by allowing previously generated tokens to be revised during sampling, thereby shaping the coupling between successive sampling states. Despite its growing role in sampler design, this coupling freedom remains insufficiently characterized. We introduce Activity Geometry to study these finite-step couplings through expected transition cost, which we call activity. We show that activity decomposes into the minimum required by the induced marginal transport and an excess term arising from the coupling. Using this minimum as a reference, we propose Minimal-Activity Finite-Time Coupling (MAFTC) to realize prescribed marginals with minimum activity without retraining or additional model evaluations. In the continuous-time limit, the minimum activity per unit time converges to the minimum expected jump rate compatible with the prescribed path. For metric-induced Gibbs paths, we further show that the activity of the kinetic-optimal flux admits a geometric decomposition. We find that total activity alone can obscure coupling excess: a sampler may approach the minimum activity required by the prescribed marginal transport while still retaining substantial coupling excess. In language generation, as the number of model evaluations increases, refinement-based samplers accumulate additional trajectory activity with limited diversity gains, whereas MAFTC reduces trajectory activity while maintaining comparable generation quality and higher lexical diversity.

candidates.title: Validating Multi-Model AI-Generated Acceptance Criteria in Requirements Engineering
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in software engineering to generate artifacts such as requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, documentation, and code. Their use in requirements engineering raises important questions about correctness, traceability, and hallucination, especially because flawed specifications can affect later design, implementation, and verification activities. While much recent work on AI-assisted software engineering has focused on code generation and code-level validation, the validation of AI-generated specifications has received less attention. This paper addresses this gap by presenting a validation-oriented approach for AI-generated acceptance criteria. The approach combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), multi-model generation, and an explicitly structured human-in-the-loop workflow. We describe a working prototype that allows users to prepare or enter user stories, generate acceptance criteria using several LLMs, optionally augment generation with retrieved requirements-related examples, compare outputs side by side, inspect retrieved context, and select, edit, or regenerate candidate criteria before explicitly submitting a reviewer-finalized version. The system also records model outputs, user interventions, retrieval settings, and final criteria as part of a logged decision process. Rather than claiming that generation accuracy is already improved, the contribution of this work is to operationalize validation as an explicit, inspectable, and accountable process for AI-generated requirements artifacts.
candidates.comment: Accepted for publication in the proceedings of VeriFAI 2026, Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS). Official publication forthcoming

candidates.title: Metamorphic Testing of Learned Spatial Surrogates for Transit Accessibility
candidates.abstract: Transit-network design requires evaluating many candidates, but detailed accessibility calculations are too slow to repeat inside an optimization loop. We therefore train a neural surrogate to approximate them. Given a candidate bus network and fixed information about rail service and nearby opportunities, it predicts the calculated spatial change in accessibility. We compare its predictions with routing-derived targets in geographically held-out regions and test specified qualitative relations under controlled input changes. Reference calculations on constructed networks assess the applicability of relations that have a routing-level counterpart. Models with positive predictive skill can still fail basic connectivity tests. One targeted intervention substantially increases pass rates for two connectivity relations while predictive skill also improves. Average prediction error is therefore insufficient when a learned model becomes an optimization objective. Predictive agreement and controlled behavioral tests should be reported separately.

candidates.title: From the ELBO to Maximum Likelihood: Convergence of Variational Autoencoders for Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Modeling
candidates.abstract: Nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) models are the central statistical models of pharmacometrics, where they support dose selection, individualized dosing and regulatory decisions in drug development. Statistically, NLME modeling is a marginalized likelihood problem. Variational autoencoders (VAEs) solve such problems with a neural network encoder that amortizes the approximation of the intractable posterior distribution, and allow the integration of AI components into NLME modeling. This paper provides the convergence analysis of the VAE-NLME algorithm. First, its version for the evidence lower bound (ELBO) is proven to converge almost surely to the set of stationary points of the ELBO, without assuming that the encoder is trained exactly. Second, the final VAE-NLME algorithm trains the encoder on the ELBO by gradient-based optimization and uses it as proposal for importance-weighted sufficient statistics. It converges almost surely to the set of stationary points of the marginal log-likelihood, without any assumption on the training of the encoder. Thus, it combines the fast gradient-based training of VAEs with the limit of maximum likelihood estimation.

candidates.title: Decision Models: An Introduction and Capability Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Applications such as ticket routing and incident triage need decisions that software can act on. Decision models provide these outputs through explicit types for choices, binary judgments, and policy scores. We evaluate the accuracy, output validity, and request latency of eleven configurations on 1,000 English and Chinese cases across nine task suites. StartLux Instant achieves 95.3% overall accuracy, returns valid outputs on all 1,000 cases, and has a median request latency of 0.084 s. It reaches 99.4% on classification and routing and selects the correct response on all 100 tool-selection cases. The highest overall accuracy among the evaluated configurations is 97.1%. These results show how a typed decision service can support fast, programmatic decisions and why its suitability depends on task-specific errors and latency requirements.

candidates.title: The Control-Flow Tax: Specialized Decision Routing for LLM Agent Workflows
candidates.abstract: An agent can spend almost as much deciding what to do as doing it. In our documentation workflow, control-flow routing accounts for 42.5% of baseline reference cost on the initial task. Lower token prices alone do not solve this control-flow tax: inexpensive general-purpose routers can trigger additional calls to the expensive generator. We evaluate a heterogeneous architecture in which Jev, a specialized System 1 decision model, controls finite actions while Sol generates documents. Across four software tasks, 480 valid runs comprise 470 completions and ten request-limit endpoints. Jev full routing achieves the lowest mean cost and elapsed time on every task, completing all 40 specialist-controlled runs along the shortest trajectory. On the initial task, mean cost falls by 49.6% (95% paired-bootstrap interval: 42.9% to 56.3%) and elapsed time by 33.2% (19.6% to 46.7%). Across three further tasks, cost reductions are 40.5% to 42.9% and concurrent elapsed-time reductions are 12.9% to 14.4%. Existence-only specialization saves just 1.8% on the initial task. Separately, Sol and Jev each select accepted actions on 100/100 reviewed retail states, with Jev using 97.88% less reference cost and 72.30% less mean request time. The results identify two requirements for efficient agent control: inexpensive decisions and trajectories that preserve those savings.
candidates.comment: 20 pages, 4 figures, 9 tables. Shuanghu Wang and Li Jiang share second authorship

candidates.title: Implementation of Machine Translation for the Uzbek Language Based on Transformer Models
candidates.abstract: This research focuses on building a machine translation system for the Uzbek language using transformer models such as T5 and mT5. Because of the limited data and the complexity of the Uzbek language, we collect, preprocess and augment data to create a strong Uzbek-English parallel corpus of about 3 million sentence pairs. The models are fine-tuned for optimal translation performance, and we use the BLEU score to evaluate the results. This study shows that our approach significantly improves upon older methods and helps promote the Uzbek language in the digital world.
candidates.comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Authors' version of a paper published in the Proceedings of the 1st International Scientific-Practical Conference "Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence: Problems, Innovations and Trends" (DTAI-2024), Tashkent State University of Economics, pp. 450-456; reference list corrected and figures redrawn

candidates.title: CriticJEPA: World Models Are Better Critics Than Optimizers
candidates.abstract: Visual world models enable goal-directed planning by predicting action outcomes. Gradient-based planners optimize actions to lower predicted goal cost, but continued optimization can exploit prediction errors after execution stops improving. Comparing plans requires informative relative scores; improving them also requires reliable update directions. Exact-state execution reveals that a frozen hierarchical world model ranks goal-conditioned proposals even when its rankings among outputs of prolonged gradient search are uninformative. Effective planning pairs goal-directed candidates with predictions that distinguish their outcomes. We introduce CriticJEPA, which learns goal-conditioned flow proposals from reward-free trajectories and uses frozen rollouts to select among them at every hierarchy level. Forward selection forms a complete planner; short anchored updates refine candidates before selection. Across visual navigation and manipulation, CriticJEPA increases success at a fraction of the planning compute, transferring shared settings across independently trained models, hierarchy depths, and unseen tasks while keeping every world-model weight fixed.

candidates.title: Any2Act: Scaling In-Context Robot Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrations
candidates.abstract: Robot in-context learning (ICL) enables a policy to perform unseen tasks by following contextual demonstrations, without task-specific fine-tuning. This is increasingly valuable as large language models reasoning at low frequency can specify tasks through demonstrations and delegate high-frequency execution to such a policy. However, methods conditioned on human videos are bounded by scarce human-robot pairs, while those conditioned on robot demonstrations accept only one or two source types at limited scale. We present Any2Act, a foundation model for robot ICL. Our key insight is that a demonstration should be expressed in the camera layout and action space of the robot that performs it (the executor), not of whoever provided it (the demonstrator). This unified embodiment-grounded representation decouples learning to follow from admitting a new source. Any2Act learns to follow once, from robot-to-robot pairs that already take this form in 1.2M real trajectories spanning 10K tasks. Human videos, simulation, UMI, and other robots are then translated into this representation, and source-routed adapters trained on only a few hundred pairs each absorb the residual gap while the pretrained model stays frozen. For long horizons, a training-free tracker feeds only the demonstration window around the executor's progress, bounding the context and rolling back to redo failed steps. From a single demonstration, Any2Act achieves 57.5% success on unseen tasks without fine-tuning, exceeding VLAs fine-tuned on 50 demonstrations per task; other demonstrators retain 74-91% of the success achieved with the executor's own demonstrations.

candidates.title: Beyond Hard Tokens: Predictive Memory for Multimodal Protein Generation
candidates.abstract: Multimodal protein language models unify sequence and discrete structural tokens via iterative masked decoding, offering a promising paradigm for joint protein design. However, standard decoders rely on a memoryless mask reset at each iteration: only a sparse subset of newly committed hard tokens is carried forward, while all remaining unresolved sites are reset to an identical [MASK] embedding. In open-ended co-generation where neither modality provides a fixed external anchor, this stateless transition limits single-step refinement depth and deprives both tracks of stable cross-step soft anchors, leading to slow convergence or degenerative repetitive collapse. Observing that uncommitted predictions evolve with pronounced temporal coherence rather than erratic noise, we introduce Predictive Memory (PredMem), a training-free self-conditioning recurrence that carries these soft beliefs across steps. At each step, PredMem summarizes raw logits into a probability-weighted Top-$k$ expectation embedding at every residue and affinely interpolates it into eligible masked inputs on the next step at zero extra denoiser cost. Across DPLM-2, DPLM-2.1, and ESM3, PredMem raises unconditional sequence-structure co-generation success by 3.6, 17.7, and 48.7 percentage points, respectively, while improving the quality-diversity trade-off and suppressing repetitive mode collapse. Controlled diagnostics show that these gains stem primarily from early trajectory stabilization in unanchored cross-modal co-evolution rather than extra compute or simple entropy reduction, establishing PredMem as an efficient inference mechanism for multimodal discrete generation.

candidates.title: When Exact Token Importance Is Not Enough: Limits of Top-K Selection in LLM Attention
candidates.abstract: Long-context language models often retain only a limited set of past token positions for an attention query. A common strategy scores positions individually and keeps the highest-ranked K. Yet attention weights are renormalized over the chosen set: two individually important positions need not form the best pair. We ask whether independent ranking suffices even when each importance score measures the exact downstream change in next-token predictions caused by deleting that position alone. It does not. A four-position construction makes the ranked pair incur 133.2 times the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence of the optimal pair, and a parametric family proves that this multiplicative gap is unbounded. An exact exchange identity and preference reversals for every K >= 2 explain the interaction. In exhaustive frozen-model audits of SmolLM2, Gemma, and Qwen, exact-singleton Top-4 leaves at least 10% relative improvement within a fully enumerated 24-position candidate pool in 55/60, 49/60, and 60/60 cases, respectively. SwapCert, a same-budget one-swap audit, detects 157/164 such cases and returns directly checkable improving supports. A KL-margin certificate relates support fidelity to next-token stability; larger-budget, multi-layer cached-decoding experiments measure predictive fidelity at K = 128 and 256. These results establish joint support quality as an essential object of analysis for sparse attention and motivate downstream-aware support selection under inference constraints.

candidates.title: FigmaEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating AI Agents in Professional UI Design
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in AI agents have enabled autonomous UI design using professional tools such as Figma, yet evaluating their design capabilities remains challenging due to the open-ended nature of design tasks and the absence of unique ground truths. We introduce FigmaEval, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on professional UI design tasks, comprising 84 tasks and 783 screens derived from real-world Figma design files. FigmaEval adopts a constrained-specification, open-solution paradigm, standardizing task requirements and design resources while allowing agents to independently determine layouts, visual hierarchies, component composition, and visual presentation. To assess design quality beyond reference similarity, we develop 22 expert-grounded evaluation rubrics across six dimensions and introduce a human evaluation arena where professional designers compare agent-generated designs through blinded pairwise judgments. Evaluating eleven models under a unified Figma agent setup, we find substantial agreement between rubric-based assessments and human preferences, alongside distinct differences in design practices and quality--efficiency trade-offs. FigmaEval provides a framework for systematically assessing professional UI design capabilities and understanding the strengths and limitations of current AI agents.

candidates.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations
candidates.abstract: Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of the continuation monad proposed to address the inefficiencies associated with the selection monad in alpha-beta search. We illustrate our approach with an implementation of Tic-Tac-Toe, observing a 39-fold reduction in the number of plays evaluated, compared with exhaustive search, in computing an optimal play. Finally, we formally establish the correctness of our construction by proving that the monadic alpha-beta search computes the same optimal outcomes and plays as exhaustive minimax search. Our results demonstrate how a foundational algorithm in AI can be expressed and verified using standard monadic abstractions, providing a basis for further development of compositional approaches to adversarial search.

candidates.title: SPRUNN: Structural Proximity for Pruning in Deep Neural Networks
candidates.abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have demonstrated significant accuracy across various machine learning tasks. However, these networks suffer from a huge number of parameters and computations, which leads to time-consuming processes. Consequently, parameter pruning approaches have been proposed to compress DNNs and efficiently implement them. The main challenge in pruning is selecting the appropriate parameters for pruning without significantly damaging the accuracy. In this paper, we propose SPRUNN, an algorithmic pruning approach based on the structural proximity criterion for filter pruning in convolutional layers of deep neural networks. Structural Proximity (SP) calculates filter similarity by considering all filters and comparing each one with the others, effectively identifying less important filters for pruning in the convolutional layers. Furthermore, we integrate this approach with fine-grained pruning in Fully Connected(FC)layerstocompresstheDNNsthatinclude both convolutional and FC layers.Toenhancetheaccuracyoftheprunedmodel,weproposealearning rate refinement strategy during the retraining phase. Experimental results demonstrate that SPRUNN achieves significant compression with high accuracy across diverse architectures and datasets.

candidates.title: Putting a Robot on a Phone Call: Layered Signaling, Bounded Occupancy and Turn Arbitration over WebRTC
candidates.abstract: We put a Thor robot on a browser voice call, with speech sent from Safari, answers played through the robot's loudspeaker and transcripts returned to the phone. We separate HTTPS signaling, relayed WebRTC media and speech generation into independently observable routes. The browser prefetches relay credentials and allows a 500 ms window after its first relay candidate. The backend starts speech and WebRTC-answer preparation concurrently within a 55 s deadline. A session slot and a non-blocking speaker lock coordinate calls with local voice access. A 2 s gate gives the controller an opportunity to suppress chat before playback. Fifteen of sixteen first dials reached ready-to-speak, comprising seven of eight Wi-Fi calls with a median of 5.57 s and eight of eight cellular calls with a median of 6.76 s. All twenty scored occupancy and recovery scenarios admitted a later call. During five 60 s outages, the backend released the line while the phone remained offline. Across 40 controlled replays, enabling the gate suppressed chat when the controller decided at 1 s. At 3 s, chat and controller feedback both played in sequence, with no overlapping output in any trace. Two additional boundary traces exposed a receipt naming a later feedback item and a new call's query returning its predecessor's feedback. These measurements cover application events on one platform and simulated controller decisions, with acoustic output and task correctness outside their scope.

candidates.title: Sparse Poison, Strong Hijack: Efficient Trajectory-Level Backdoors in Vision-Language-Action Models with Only 1\% Poisoning
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models advance robotic manipulation, but their reliance on demonstrations exposes them to backdoor threats. Among these threats, trajectory-level targeted backdoors are particularly challenging and may pose greater safety risks than behavior-disrupting attacks: rather than merely causing task failures or local action deviations, they must sustain closed-loop redirection to complete an attacker-specified multi-step task. To reliably induce such behaviors, existing methods typically rely on high poisoning rates to obtain sufficient target-trajectory supervision. However, high poisoning rates may compromise clean-task performance, whereas low rates leave target-trajectory supervision scarce and backdoor learning vulnerable to interference from dominant clean-task updates. To resolve this trade-off at low poisoning rates, we propose a two-stage co-optimization framework guided by vision, language, and action. Stage I freezes the policy and uses differentiable rendering and multimodal supervision to optimize a 3D trigger's texture, translation, and scale, strengthening trigger-target associations from limited poisoned demonstrations. Building on the optimized trigger, Stage II applies source-selective dual-LoRA adaptation to decouple clean and backdoor updates and mitigate their interference, followed by learned column-wise calibration and analytic fusion into a unified policy. Experiments on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, $π_0$, and $π_{0.5}$ across four LIBERO suites show consistent gains over all evaluated attack baselines. With only 1% poisoned data, our method achieves 86.4% target success and 95.2% clean-task success on OpenVLA-OFT in LIBERO-Spatial. Real-robot trials also demonstrate trajectory-level hijacking.
candidates.comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, including supplementary material. Simin Huang and Jiawei Chen contributed equally. Code: https://github.com/vla-attack/Sparse_Poison_Strong_Hijack

candidates.title: ArabFake: A multitask deep learning framework for Arabic fake news Detection, Categorization, and risk prediction
candidates.abstract: The spread of fake news among Arabic media including social media represents a great challenge to the integrity of information and the trust of the public in it. In this paper, we introduce a comprehensive deep-learning framework, named ArabFake, that goes beyond the binary classification on Arabic fake news detection. ArabFake, built over MARBERTv2 (a state-of-the-art model for multi-dialectal Arabic tweets), proficiently address the complexity of the Arabic language while performing three unified tasks which are fake news detection, content categorization and its risk assessment. The framework promotes efficiency and performance both by enabling multi-task learning through shared knowledge representation across tasks. In order to facilitate development and evaluation, we present the ArabFake Dataset consisting of 2,495 manually labelled news items with labels that are verified by experts regarding fake news categories and risk levels. ArabFake demonstrates robust performance, achieving an F1 score of 94.12% for fake news detection, 84.92% for categorization, and 88.91% for risk zone assessment, highlighting its reliability and effectiveness across multiple tasks. We improve interpretability and extract insight into manipulative techniques by integrating valence scoring as part of the framework that emphasizes misleading linguistic cues used to disseminate fake news within the produced image. The results show that ArabFake is a holistic Arabic fake news detection framework that has practical implications on news organizations and fact checking projects.

candidates.title: DAiSy: Online Data Selection by Adaptive Utility Estimation for LLM Pretraining
candidates.abstract: Model-aware online data selection prioritizes the training documents that contribute the most given the model's current state. Existing online selectors rank candidates upon gradient-based data utility scores, which requires the full forward-backward pass of the main model on every candidate document. Scoring each document therefore pays as much as training on it, yet only a small fraction is used for the real model update. We introduce DAiSy, a lightweight linear auxiliary model that learns to predict data utility scores from frozen document embeddings, which eliminates the computation overhead and infrastructure burdens. The linear estimator is updated alongside the main language model, fitting to the exact gradient-based utility scores obtained from the backward pass of regular training steps. Consequently, scoring a candidate requires only a linear transformation, bypassing the costly gradient-alignment computation. We demonstrate its effectiveness and efficiency for LLM pretraining in English and multilingual scenarios, with various steering target designs. The improvements from DAiSy can consistently survive the instruction-tuning phase.

candidates.title: VC-OPD: Learning to See What Matters via Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation
candidates.abstract: Visual On-Policy Distillation (OPD) commonly uses cropped or zoomed-in image regions as teacher-side privileged information to improve fine-grained perception in small Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). However, local pixel-level cues are insufficient for complex visual reasoning that requires global structure, spatial relationships, and high-level semantics. We propose Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation (VC-OPD), which extends teacher-side privileged information beyond local image regions to question-conditioned visual cues. Advanced MLLMs generate cues capturing key visual details, structural relationships, and semantic evidence needed to answer each question. A multi-stage quality filtering process selects reliable cues, which are provided only to the teacher during training. This enables informative token-level supervision along student-generated trajectories, helping the student learn to identify and reason over critical evidence directly from the original image. No additional information is required at inference time. Since advanced MLLMs are used only for visual cue generation, VC-OPD is compatible with both open-weight and proprietary black-box models. Experiments on STEM and general visual reasoning benchmarks show consistent improvements across model scales over reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation baselines. Notably, a 4B model trained with VC-OPD outperforms many baselines with 8B or more parameters, demonstrating effective capability transfer through question-conditioned visual cues.

candidates.title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
candidates.abstract: Solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) over long time horizons is computationally expensive using traditional numerical methods. While neural operators provide an efficient alternative, they suffer from the accumulation of approximation errors along the predicted trajectory, typically caused by the failure to capture fine-scale details. In this work, we design a Commutator Memory Neural Operator that identifies fine-scale dynamical details by commuting two operations and leverages these details to enhance the neural operator's capability in capturing fine-scale features over long time horizons. Specifically, we identify a performance gap between two operations: downsampling the high-resolution field before rollout prediction versus performing rollout prediction before downsampling. We observe that fine-scale dynamical details are often encoded in this gap. By commuting these two operations, the fine-scale details removed during downsampling can be captured. Furthermore, we employ a memory module to store these fine-scale features along the trajectory and retrieve them during rollout, generating spatially adaptive corrections that enhance long-horizon fidelity. Empirical results across five systems demonstrate that CoMNO improves prediction accuracy and long-horizon rollout stability.
