candidates.comment: In preparing an earlier version of this manuscript under time pressure, we did not adequately verify all reported experimental results. In this preprint, we correct the numerical reporting errors we identified and update the affected analyses

candidates.title: Pando: Noise-Coupled Parallel Draft Trees for Efficient Edge Speculative Decoding
candidates.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) decoding emits one token per forward pass, reloading the full model each time, so LLM inference on edge devices is memory-bound while the compute units sit idle. Speculative decoding puts that idle compute to work by verifying several drafted tokens in a single pass. State-of-the-art parallel drafters such as DFlash and DSpark propose an entire block of draft tokens in one forward pass, which makes drafting compute-efficient. However, they are deployed with draft chains whose length is capped by the block size they are trained for, leaving most of the computational budget for verification unused. To tackle this problem, we propose Pando, which builds dynamic draft trees on top of a parallel drafter and thereby removes this cap. Pando employs noise-coupled pruning, which draws the target model's sampling noise before drafting and ranks candidate branches under that noise, so the tree retains the branches the target will actually sample. Noise coupling is lossless and requires no retraining or additional model pass, yet increases acceptance length by up to $8.4\%$ on Qwen3-8B. To optimize and evaluate Pando configurations across hardware, we normalize an operator-level roofline to AR decoding, reducing every platform to its ridge point. On a representative edge device, a 16-node Pando tree attains $5.3\times$ speedup and $4.2\times$ energy reduction over AR decoding: $25\%$ faster than DSpark's released chain, and $27\%$ faster and $72\%$ more energy-efficient than an EAGLE-3 tree. The best configurations remain memory-bound on every edge device we model, so added compute capacity does not reduce their latency.

candidates.title: Unjamming Deferrals: Supporting Students Through JAMN Bot, a Mobile RAG-Grounded Policy Assistant
candidates.abstract: In some educational institutions, workflows such as the exam deferral process can be slow, inconvenient, and inconsistent, which creates the need to implement novel digital systems. This paper presents Schedulater, a mobile app for managing university exam deferrals. JAMN Bot is a Large Language Model (LLM)-powered chatbot integrated into Schedulater that provides context-aware support to help users understand the deferral process. The system features a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline using Ollama (Llama 3.2 3B) for self-hosted inference which enables policy-grounded responses without sacrificing privacy. We evaluate the system using a 43-item benchmark spanning Exam Deferral, Privacy, Scheduling, Cross-Policy, and Adversarial & Out-of-Scope questions, and report inter-rater agreement among our human evaluators alongside retrieval hit-rate metrics. Subsequently, we utilize an LLM-as-a-judge approach with GPT-5.4, revealing slight-to-moderate alignment with our raters that improves with answer quality, and check the ranking against a panel including Gemini 3.5 Flash and Qwen3.5 397B. The results of our study display trade-offs between open-weight and frontier models, as well as LLM-human evaluation alignment with answer quality. Schedulater demonstrates the feasibility of integrating lightweight LLMs into university administrative workflows with structured retrieval.
candidates.comment: Extended version of a paper published in the proceedings of IEEE SmartEdu 2026 (2026 IEEE Smart World Congress), pp. 810-817. 12 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables. Benchmark and code: https://github.com/JAMNSoftware/jamn-rag-benchmark

candidates.title: EgoLoAF: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations with Hand-Object Affordances
candidates.abstract: Training humanoid vision-language-action (VLA) models relies heavily on costly real-robot teleoperation. Recent efforts convert egocentric human demonstrations into humanoid training data. However, most methods still require wearable motion trackers and leave important hand-object interaction cues implicit. Many also mix in real-robot teleoperation data for VLA post-training. These dependencies limit scalable data collection, while implicit interaction cues make precise contact harder to learn. To overcome these limitations, we propose EgoLoAF, the first paradigm to derive all training data for humanoid loco-manipulation directly from egocentric demonstrations without wearable motion trackers. We post-train the VLA on the converted data alone, without real-robot teleoperation demonstrations, and use explicit hand-object interaction cues to guide action generation. Specifically, to obtain humanoid action targets, we estimate torso motion from recorded camera poses and reconstruct both hand trajectories from video. From the same recording, we use each hand's current pose relative to the object to represent hand-object affordances. During post-training, we inject these affordances into the action expert through cross-attention while keeping the vision-language backbone frozen. Additionally, we release 128,400 egocentric demonstration episodes spanning 1,000 hours and 1,284 tasks, together with converted humanoid action trajectories and rendered robot-view observations. Across four real-world tasks, EgoLoAF nearly achieves teleoperation performance (73.1 vs. 74.4 in mean Task Progress Score), while achieving a mean 4.03 times improvement in data-collection efficiency.

candidates.title: Seldon TFM family: Seldon-Mini, Seldon and Seldon+
candidates.abstract: We introduce Seldon, a family of tabular foundation models. Our classifier Seldon+ ranks first among 15 models on TabBench, our benchmark of 124 classification datasets, and on its variant with missing values. In our own runs of public benchmarks, it also ranks first on BeyondArena IID classification and TabBench-Bio, and second on TabArena classification. The open-weight models Seldon-Mini (27M parameters) and Seldon (213M parameters) both lie on the TabArena Pareto front of Elo against inference time: no entry is both more accurate and faster. On TabArena, Seldon ranks fourth and Seldon-Mini seventh among 109 leaderboard entries, and on the IID track of BeyondArena, Seldon ranks second among 42 entries. Seldon-Mini and Seldon handle both classification and regression, use an architecture similar to those of Kumo-Tabular, TabFM and TabPFN-3.5, and are trained on synthetic tables only.
candidates.comment: Technical report. 18 pages, 9 figures, 6 tables. Models: https://huggingface.co/Neuralk-AI/seldon and https://huggingface.co/Neuralk-AI/seldon-mini

candidates.title: RoboDemo: Reconciling Demonstration Intent and Execution Progress for Long-Horizon Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires more than predicting the next action from the current observation. The policy must maintain a global procedural prior that specifies the expected progress of each subtask stage, while also tracking the realized progress produced by its interactions. To this end, we propose RoboDemo, a demonstration-augmented manipulation framework built on Dual-Cascaded Test-Time-Training. RoboDemo accepts either a task-relevant human demonstration video or a semantically compatible robot video retrieved from simulation corpus as reference, allowing us to evaluate its applicability with and without paired human demonstrations. Task semantics and physical motion information from the reference video are then transferred into persistent demonstration-intent memory. During deployment, we causally compress online observations, robot states, and executed actions into interaction-progress memory. To keep reference intent stable while interaction progress continually evolves, reference and execution video tokens independently update their respective fast-weight states. The action expert performs cascaded memory reads, first obtaining reference guidance and then refining it using realized progress, allowing the policy to adapt to execution deviations without overwriting the stored intent. RoboDemo achieves 90.7% success on Imitator Game and 73.3% success across three real-world household tasks. Real-world videos, code and hf-weights are available in our project website.

candidates.title: Refining and Aligning Clinical Reasoning with Health Guidelines via Formal Constraints
candidates.abstract: Clinical reasoning from incomplete or conflicting patient evidence must account for low-probability but high-risk concerns while remaining grounded in health guidelines. We introduce VerClin, an explainable framework that extracts guideline conditions, exclusions, recommendations, and priorities into executable knowledge and represents patient conversations as scoped cases. A deterministic four-valued reasoner produces traceable guideline matches while preserving uncertainty and enforcing exclusions. Multiple specialty agents then screen matched guidelines for case applicability, and a consultation model synthesizes accepted guidance through specialty recommendations and a sentence-preserving formal-constraint channel. We present accepted guidance in ascending order of the sum of its priority and trigger-strength ranks, which can surface high-risk guidance with weaker triggers. VerClin outperforms direct generation and Top-5 RAG on HealthBench Hard and HealthBench Professional. On the LLMEval-Med subset, it outperforms direct generation and ties Top-5 RAG. Component analyses further examine semantic closure, example-guided refinement, specialty screening, and constraint-conditioned delivery.

candidates.title: SkillCore: Internalizing Generalizable Skills via Scaffolding-Removed Fine-Tuning
candidates.abstract: Runtime skills can improve agents' problem-solving capabilities by providing procedural guidance for tasks such as code review and debugging. However, these benefits reach only a minority of users, as most do not proactively invoke skills in practice. We argue that such generalizable procedures should become part of the model's capabilities rather than remain optional external add-ons, making them directly available without explicit skill loading. To this end, we present SkillCore, a data pipeline and supervised fine-tuning recipe for internalizing generalizable skills. We transform real agent trajectories by removing skill-loading scaffolding while preserving the task context and subsequent agent actions, thereby supervising direct execution without external skill content. To preserve access to task-specific skills that provide genuinely external information, we mix these scaffold-removed trajectories with a small proportion of skill-native trajectories that preserve supervision for skill invocation. On a held-out skill-free evaluation, SkillCore improves task completion quality over the base Qwen3-8B and Qwen2.5-72B models by 54.4% and 24.8%, respectively, while preserving task-specific skill invocation on a separate probe and general coding performance on SWE-bench Verified.

candidates.title: VLAs Execute, Code Recovers: 3D Skill Envelopes Bridge the Compositional Gap in Agentic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Composing frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) skills under an agentic planner promises scalable long-horizon manipulation without long-horizon demonstrations, yet strong atomic skills routinely fail at seams even under a correct plan. Standard remedies reset the robot's pose or draft entry conditions in language, missing the physical cause we uncover via causal interventions: even after re-homing, a frozen VLA rigidly retraces its habitual trajectory and collides with displaced scene residue, whether or not it can see it. We propose the Skill Envelope, a policy-measured 3D geometric precondition capturing the volume a frozen skill sweeps during successful executions. Exploiting the insight that the rigidity making a frozen skill fragile at seams also makes its trajectory predictable in advance, we expose each envelope as two classical 3D tools (CHECK to detect blocking residue and FREE to locate safe placement regions), establishing a division of labor where VLAs execute in-distribution manipulation and code repairs out-of-distribution states. On LIBERO-Goal with frozen $π_{0.5}$, our zero-failure envelope predicts collisions at 0.946 AUROC (0.944 from one RGB-D view) and beats frontier VLMs on seam readiness (0.902 vs. 0.793); using it for skill ordering and code repair lifts success from 82.8% to 92.3% on two-step seams and from 29.7% to 93.8% on drawer-bearing 3-4 step chains, matching privileged world reset. Together, these results show that reliable VLA composition hinges on measuring a policy's physical workspace rather than guessing preconditions in language. Ongoing work closes the loop with autonomous LLM orchestration, synthesized free-object recovery, and cross-policy evaluation on cluttered benchmarks and real hardware.

candidates.title: Motion Chain of Thought: Disentangling Motion Semantics from Visual Appearance for Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) aim to construct a unified architecture capable of understanding world state evolution and guiding action generation. However, existing visual branches focus on predicting static visual observation, rather than reflecting potential transition information that captures the evolution of world states under motion interactions. This leads to representational entanglement between high-level physical condition evolution and low-level action trajectory generation within the Action Model, creating a structural bottleneck while weakening the predictive capability of world evolution modeling for action generation. We propose PILOT (Physical Inference for Latent Optimized Trajectories), whose core Representational Deduction (RD) bridges this gap by integrating motion chain-of-thought (CoT) guidance as a native model capability. Specifically, RD aims to encourage the action branch to explicitly model potential state transition tokens, which are retained as CoT in the reasoning space to guide fine-grained motion trajectory. Experiments demonstrate that RD not only improves the success rate and generalization ability of WAMs in complex robotic manipulation tasks but also enhances the model's physical interpretability by decoupling high-level motion semantics from low-level trajectory details. Furthermore, the abundant state transition supervision signals introduced by RD effectively alleviate the sparse supervision in action generation, supporting data-efficient real-robot adaptation with reduced demonstration sets.

candidates.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Agent-orchestrated robot systems combine the general reasoning capability of multimodal agents with the precise physical control of learned visuomotor policies. Yet such systems often fail at the moment of handoff: a policy is reliable only from a limited set of start states, while the agent may invoke it outside this region. We call this region the policy's handoff boundary. Existing whole-task policies typically have handoff boundaries that are narrow and difficult for an agent to characterize, making reliable coordination challenging. We propose Boundary-Aware Policy Learning, which explicitly shapes and then expands the handoff boundary of a visuomotor policy. First, Boundary-Explicit Training fine-tunes the policy on contact segments with diverse start poses, yielding a wide and well-defined boundary that can be communicated to the agent through a simple handoff protocol. Second, Boundary-Expanding Self-Improvement retrains the policy on curated successful system rollouts, extending the boundary toward earlier stages of each task and allowing the agent to hand over sooner with fewer language-model calls. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboDojo, our system outperforms the strongest baseline by over 26 percentage points, reaching 98.4% success in randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, while further reducing its API cost and execution time by 41.3% and 37.5%, respectively. These results suggest that the key to robust agent-policy orchestration lies not only in improving either component individually, but also in explicitly shaping the boundary between them.

candidates.title: Roboclock: A Unified Benchmark for Time-Aware Robotic Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Time is a fundamental dimension of robotic intelligence: a robot may fail despite physically correct actions if it acts outside a valid time window, responds too slowly to an event, or fails to meet required throughput. Yet existing robotic benchmarks primarily emphasize spatial correctness and logical task completion, largely overlooking the temporal constraints of real-world applications. We present RoboClock, a unified benchmark for time-aware robotic manipulation featuring 60 tasks across five application domains. Mirroring these failure modes, RoboClock structures tasks around three types of temporal constraints: Temporal Window, Event-Reactive, and Throughput. Furthermore, RoboClock incorporates a Latency-Aligned evaluation protocol that continuously advances environment time during model inference and control-interface delays, paired with time-sensitive metrics. Evaluating over 30 methods, we find that the best-performing approach is the trained VLA, yet it achieves only 8.3% temporal success even on Easy-level tasks, with persistent challenges in generalization and transfer. These findings reveal fundamental limitations in current robotic systems and highlight the need to jointly optimize physical competence, temporal reasoning, and execution latency.

candidates.title: Disentangling Visual Dynamics for World Model Planning
candidates.abstract: Visual world models enable planning through predictive latent states. However, entangled agent and exogenous dynamics can obscure task progress. Disentangling visual dynamics for planning requires addressing two challenges: 1) suppressing cross-factor interference while retaining useful information; and 2) linking factors to task-relevant signals, since stability alone does not ensure meaningful planning distances. Therefore, we introduce FactorWorld, a disentangled visual dynamics framework for world model planning. To separate agent and exogenous dynamics, we propose a Counterfactual Consensus Residual Factorizer (CCRF) guided by bidirectional counterfactual pairs. CCRF separates shared context from dynamic residuals, combining average and worst-partner constraints to suppress interference with state and motion supervision to retain useful information. To translate these factors into planning decisions, we introduce semantic routing to refine full-representation task predictions for state estimation, trajectory scoring, and task-adapted planning. Experiments on MiniGrid, MetaDrive, and CARLA show improved bidirectional factor stability across two backbones. On MiniGrid, factor routing raises mean SR from 78.80% to 82.40%. Across four continuous control tasks, including Push-T, FactorWorld achieves mean success rates ranging from 91.67% to 100% across tasks. These results demonstrate that combining decoupled visual dynamics with explicit tasks can significantly improve the planning capabilities of world models.

candidates.title: Joint Classification and Generation on Tabular Data: an Empirical Study
candidates.abstract: Many applications of machine learning on tabular data need both a classifier and a generator of realistic records. The default is to train two separate models, whereas a single joint model promises both from one set of weights. Several families of tabular deep learning models can be turned into such a joint model, which raises the question of which joint model is preferable at which computational budget. In this empirical study, we introduce and compare joint models based on four state-of-the-art tabular data modeling families (energy-based models, probabilistic circuits, tabular foundation models and tabular diffusion models) against measured FLOPs and wall-clock time, on 29 classification datasets. Methods are evaluated based on two defined aggregate scores that take into account different aspects of prediction and generation. We then also compare these joint models with every pair of a separate classifier and generator at different computational budgets, to see when a joint model may be a defendible choice against the regular practice of keeping a separate classifier and generator. We find that the best joint model is a probabilistic circuit at the smallest budgets and, beyond that, a tabular foundation model that generates column by column using a regressor (TabICL). Compared with pairs of separate models, this study finds a joint model is rarely preferable but often very close to the best pair, without the hassle of training and maintaining two separate models.

candidates.title: PoseVLN: Learning Geometric State Evolution for Vision-Language Navigation
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to relate past experience, current spatial state, and future motion while following natural-language instructions. Recent approaches improve these capabilities through long-horizon memory, state-aware reasoning, and future prediction, yet these components are often modeled separately, leaving navigation state evolution insufficiently connected across time. We argue that camera pose provides a natural geometric representation for bridging past, present, and future states. Based on this insight, we propose PoseVLN, a pose-aware VLN framework that jointly learns navigation decisions and geometric state evolution. PoseVLN organizes visual memory and the current observation in an episode-relative coordinate frame, and jointly predicts the next K navigation actions together with a local $Δ$Pose over the same horizon. The predicted $Δ$Pose is composed with the current trajectory-level pose to obtain the future pose state, which is recursively propagated throughout navigation, forming a continuous geometric state evolution from past memory to future motion. Experiments on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE Val-Unseen splits demonstrate the effectiveness of explicitly modeling geometric state evolution, with PoseVLN outperforming the strongest compared baselines by 2.6 and 2.9 percentage points in success rate, respectively, using only single RGB observations.
candidates.comment: 26 pages, 6 figures, including appendix. Project page: https://houpengyu123.github.io/PoseVLN/

candidates.title: ArEssays: Towards Robust Arabic Handwritten Text Understanding in Educational Settings
candidates.abstract: Automated understanding of handwritten Arabic student essays remains challenging due to script complexity and high variability in children's writing. We introduce ArEssays, a large-scale dataset of authentic essays from primary to secondary students across Egypt, with both verbatim transcriptions and linguistically corrected versions. We benchmark 34 vision-language and OCR models, including fine-tuned systems, and find large performance gaps on real student handwriting. We release the dataset, training pipelines, and results to support research in Arabic OCR, document understanding, and educational NLP.

candidates.title: XMind: Thinking Twice via Cross-Memory Reasoning for LLM-Based Autonomous Driving
candidates.abstract: Memory-augmented large language model (LLM) driving agents can reuse past experience, yet previously learned corrections often fail to transfer when traffic conditions change. A key limitation is that existing memories mainly record observed outcomes, providing little evidence about alternative actions. We introduce XMind, a training-free framework that enables LLM-based driving to "Think Twice" through cross-memory reasoning. XMind integrates working memory of recent traffic states with episodic memory of critical risk events. The agent first makes an initial decision from the current context and then cross-checks it against retrieved historical experience. If a conflict arises, it makes a second decision guided by the retrieved evidence. To construct reliable episodic memory, XMind evaluates alternative actions through counterfactual rollouts under perturbed traffic conditions and stores the verified outcomes as structured risk capsules. These capsules are retrieved by jointly matching spatial risk patterns and scenario semantics. Across closed-loop highway simulations, XMind achieves success rates of 83.3-93.3%, exceeding the strong baseline by 6.6 percentage points on average. Evaluation on K-Risk further demonstrates lower decision risk on unseen real-world high-risk interactions. Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of working memory, risk-text retrieval, and counterfactual verification. Code is available at https://github.com/xiangxiangliuwo/XMind

candidates.title: OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval
candidates.abstract: Multimodal retrieval must match dense pages, fine-grained entities, ordered video, and agent tools and memory. Single-vector embeddings lose local evidence, cross-encoders reread every recalled item online, and uncompressed late interaction is too large to serve. We present OmniEVIE, a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model covering text, images, visual documents, video, and tools with one compressed index and a three-stage retriever. Each record stores at most 128 int8 vectors of dimension 64 (9,472 bytes, or 8.82 GiB per million records), providing a mean vector, 1-bit signs, and int8 multi-vectors for coarse, middle, and final search while localizing each hit to a page region or video interval. Training, merging, indexing, and retrieval are co-designed: all tasks share one retrieval format, a three-grade evidence check removes false negatives, dynamic sampling follows the baseline-teacher gap, candidates are compressed with ST-HAC during training to match the index, stage-wise and specialist models are merged by parameter block, and a saliency gate with a noise floor refines query scoring. Trained on public datasets, OmniEVIE scores 60.68 (full d=2048 sequence) and 60.06 (K128 x d64 int8 index) on MMEB-V3 (190 tasks), 77.96 on MMEB-V2 (78 tasks), and 62.96 on ViDoRe V3 (48 tasks). On 1M and 5M records, a single-thread query takes 54.2 ms and 120.2 ms (11.1x and 25.3x faster than exact 4096-d single-vector search; 236x and 532x faster than full int8 MaxSim). Video is encoded directly from frames without a parsing model: on QVHighlights (1,083 queries), the peak falls inside the labeled segment for 78.0% of queries and the returned span (18% of video length) intersects it for 94.3% vs. 44.9% random. Weights and code: https://huggingface.co/tencent/OmniEVIE-4B and https://github.com/Tencent/OmniEVIE.

candidates.title: Who gets the information? An $α$-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection
candidates.abstract: Recent information-theoretic filters for multi-label feature selection disagree on how to distribute relevance over labels: some amplify features that inform a few labels, others balance what every label receives. We show these choices are implicit social welfare functions. Treating labels as agents whose utility is the information they receive, we propose FLIC, which greedily maximises the $α$-fair welfare of per-label information coverage. A single parameter $α$ moves from utilitarian ($α=0$) through proportionally fair ($α=1$) to max-min selection ($α\to\infty$), and a dozen published relevance terms lie on this axis, most as special cases, first-order approximations or limits. The objective is monotone submodular for every $α\ge0$ whenever each label's information is, so greedy selection is a $(1-1/e)$-approximation; this fails for $α<0$, and the max-min limit is inapproximable. Fano's and the Hellman-Raviv inequalities tie raw coverage to the Bayes Hamming loss and normalised coverage to per-label relative error. FLIC uses bias-corrected, label-wise conditional information and has no relevance-redundancy trade-off parameter. On 22 data sets, FLIC is the best of 14 information-theoretic filters on seven of nine metrics, winning 86 of 117 pairwise comparisons significantly and losing none significantly. Among 17 methods it ranks first on ranking loss, coverage and macro-AUC with two classifiers and has the best mean rank (narrowly with ML-kNN), while three embedded methods lead on Hamming loss, one-error and micro-F1.
candidates.comment: 25 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Supplementary material is provided as an ancillary file

candidates.title: Steerable by Design: Conditional Pretraining for Robust Control of Language Models
candidates.abstract: Our goal is to build language models that are steerable by design. Today's language models are pretrained with next-token prediction, which relegates alignment and control to the final 1% of training tokens or inference-time interventions. These models repurpose a single input channel for both instructions and data, leading to common failure modes where the model mistakenly treats data as instructions such as intentional jailbreaks and unintentional in-context alignment drift. To correct this, we propose a pretraining method and architecture that separates the two from the very start, producing Mancelle-3B. An encoder processes high-level semantic features of upcoming text with cross-attention that prevents the token stream from writing back into this control channel. During pretraining, the model learns to rely on these features to predict the next token, turning the channel into an effective handle for steering the model. Mancelle-3B steers more strongly than prompt- and activation-based methods on comparable open models while maintaining fluency, and it withstands adversarial black-box and soft-prompt counter-steering that defeats those baselines. We reproduce this against a more controlled baseline with Mancelle-400M. Our results show that robust control can be built into language models if we do so early and intentionally.

candidates.title: SkillHarness: Execution-Aware Coordination with Plug-and-Play Skills for Long-Horizon Traversal
candidates.abstract: Traversing complex terrain requires robots to coordinate diverse locomotion skills while adapting to unseen obstacles and changing environments. Although perceptive reinforcement learning enables agile locomotion, conventional multi-terrain locomotion rely on fixed policy, limiting adaptability and skill extensibility. Perceptual disturbances and unreliable skill transitions further challenge robust execution. To address these challenges, we propose SkillHarness, an execution-aware coordination framework that integrates a flexible, plug-and-play locomotion skill library. To enhance traversal robustness, we introduce a perceptive reinforcement learning approach that preserves task-relevant environmental references while continuously updating proprioceptive feedback, reducing sensitivity to perceptual fluctuations. A vision-language-guided Harness coordinates navigation and skill execution through event-triggered reasoning, geometric feasibility verification, and execution-phase constraints. By flexibly composing and extending available skills, SkillHarness adapts to unseen terrain and task combinations without retraining the locomotion policies. The framework further incorporates execution feedback and retrospective decision revision to improve skill selection and avoid inappropriate skill switching. We evaluate SkillHarness across diverse terrain configurations, perceptual disturbances, and multi-obstacle traversal tasks to assess its adaptability and reliability in long-horizon traversal.

candidates.title: OVOK: A Recursive Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Video-Based Articulated Robot State Estimation
candidates.abstract: Recovering articulated robot state from video supports metric spatial sensing for manipulation, scene reconstruction, and action planning. Yet the problem is ill-posed: different intrinsics, camera-to-robot poses, and joint angles can explain similar observations. Prior task-specific regressors typically assume known intrinsics, fit one robot through laborious data collection and robot-specific training, and still transfer poorly across scenes. Foundation models apply to any robot zero-shot, but their estimates have large errors. We present OVOK (One Video to Kinetics), a recursive self-improving agentic framework for this task. Under a human-authored protocol, an agentic initializer constructs robot-specific OVOK-4k; a proposer--executor--verifier loop then jointly evolves tools and executable workflows from feedback. Updated tools and workflows are accepted only when the verifier judges a positive improvement. The retained workflow is frozen for accurate inference. Experiments demonstrate that the evolved workflow achieves state-of-the-art results on DREAM-V and RoboKeyGen-V, delivering robust and accurate estimates.
candidates.comment: 24 pages, including appendix. Submitted to CVPR 2027

candidates.title: Wind-Aware Trajectory Planning for Deformable Aerial Formations
candidates.abstract: Coordinated aerial transport in dense urban environments requires drone formations to navigate confined spaces and adapt to spatially varying winds around buildings. Formation deformation enables passage through narrow spaces but changes individual drone velocities and the local winds they encounter, coupling formation motion with aerodynamic effects. We propose Family-Air, a wind-aware trajectory-family planner that constructs a virtual tube as shared collision-free flight space and jointly optimizes formation-center motion, deformation, and timing. A shared affine transformation represents a continuous trajectory family, incorporating spatially varying wind and deformation-induced velocities into a unified air-relative motion objective. The optimization enforces virtual-tube containment, inter-drone separation, and kinematic feasibility. Simulations across four urban wind-field scenarios demonstrate the importance of local wind-deformation coupling. Flight simulations further show improvements in trajectory tracking accuracy. These results demonstrate the potential of wind-aware trajectory-family planning for coordinated aerial transport in complex urban environments.

candidates.title: A Unified Control Framework for Gradient Inversion Defense in Federated Learning
candidates.abstract: Gradient perturbations are widely recognized as an effective defense against gradient inversion attacks in federated learning, but they are equally known to impair optimization, creating a persistent tension between privacy and utility. In this paper, we show that existing gradient perturbation defenses, despite their different formulations, can be unified under a controlled dynamics framework, providing a cohesive understanding of their optimization behavior and enabling the derivation of universal convergence and safety conditions without relying on case-specific analyses. Leveraging this observation, we propose ``Near Orthogonal Gradient Projection (NODE)'', which injects perturbations only along directions orthogonal to the original gradient so that the defended gradient maintains a fixed cosine similarity with the true gradient. By preserving the first-order descent direction, NODE substantially reduces the optimization cost of strong perturbations while maintaining effective protection against gradient inversion attacks. We theoretically establish convergence guarantees under standard optimization assumptions and further show that, under mild conditions on the gradient distribution, NODE remains effective in preventing inversion attacks. Comprehensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and Chest X-ray, together with a variety of gradient inversion attacks, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an improved privacy--utility trade-off over existing defenses across a broad range of training settings.

candidates.title: Multi-view Random-set Learning
candidates.abstract: Trusted multi-view learning aims to integrate heterogeneous views for accurate and reliable predictions. However, multi-view data often exhibit the view degradation phenomenon: individual views contain only partial discriminative information and cannot independently determine the instance-level label. Requiring such views to produce unambiguous class evidence can distort evidence learning and mislead subsequent fusion. Existing methods addressing this problem have at least one of the following drawbacks: (1) assigning evidence to individual classes without explicitly representing unresolved class groups; (2) projecting composite beliefs onto individual classes before fusion, preventing direct refinement of candidate groups through cross-view set intersections. To address these limitations, we propose a new Multi-view Random-Set Learning (MRSL) paradigm, which preserves view-specific support for candidate class sets and refines candidate classes through cross-view fusion. Specifically, we quantify class overlap to select a compact collection of sets for each view, avoiding the exponential cost of modeling all class subsets. We then perform set-level fusion by assigning joint support to set intersections, allowing complementary views to narrow the candidate classes before probability conversion. Experiments on synthetic and eight real-world datasets validate the proposed overlap measure and demonstrate that MRSL achieves the highest accuracy on all eight datasets. Compared with the strongest baselines, MRSL improves average accuracy by 4.71% and reduces average expected calibration error by 6.33%. All datasets and code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.
candidates.comment: 18 pages, including supplementary material. Corresponding author: Cai Xu

candidates.title: RightDiff: Learning Generative Reward Models to Judge by the Right Differences
candidates.abstract: Generative reward models typically rely on generic query-level rubrics or unconstrained rationales, overlooking the fact that pairwise preference is driven by response-specific differences. Moreover, optimizing solely for outcome correctness encourages models to exploit superficial shortcuts such as verbosity and formatting, triggering rationale drift. To address this, we propose RightDiff, which structures pairwise evaluation into an evidence-grounded evaluation trajectory executed in a single autoregressive generation. RightDiff explicitly discovers contrastive differences between candidates, categorizes them into material or immaterial factors, and induces pair-specific rubrics before final adjudication. To train this process without post-hoc rationalization, we synthesize demonstration data via response-isolated prompts and optimize the reward model with a difference-alignment reward regularized by budget-constrained one-to-one matching and multiplicative gating. RightDiff achieves state-of-the-art preference modeling performance on RewardBench and RM-Bench, surpassing all open-source reward models and leading proprietary LLM judges. Downstream, it provides reliable supervision for direct preference optimization on Arena-Hard and AlpacaEval while effectively resisting length shortcuts.

candidates.title: Reading Geometric Anchors: Viewpoint Generalization in Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation with RGB-Only Deployment
candidates.abstract: Moving the camera changes where objects appear in an image, challenging RGB-based imitation learning. A common strategy pairs synthesized views with the same demonstrated action, but ignores supporting physical correspondence across views. By predicting depth with camera calibrations, 3D policies may handle it yet suffer the issue of varied observed point sets. To address these limitations, we propose ReGeoAnch, a geometry-anchored imitation learning framework for viewpoint generalization. Specifically, we build global anchors in the robot base frame and local anchors in the gripper frame, providing shared physical references across viewpoints. Furthermore, Decoupled Appearance-Guided Geometric Readout uses Point-to-Anchor Aggregation (PAA) to obtain comparable and stable geometry around anchors beyond pointwise correspondence. A controllable and decoupled information flow, Anchor-to-Policy Readout (APR), leverages complementary visual and geometric information and supports viewpoint generalization: view-dependent appearances are queried by view-invariant robot state to select task-relevant anchors, with geometric values alone to form the final readout. We further introduce Cross-View Readout Consistency to align the directions of policy readouts from paired source and synthesized target views. Experiments on 12 manipulation tasks across MetaWorld and ManiSkill3 demonstrate improved viewpoint generalization over baseline policies.

candidates.title: Making Evaluation Explicit Is Not Enough: Supervising the Evaluation Process in Generative Reward Models
candidates.abstract: Generative reward models (GRMs) make language-model evaluation more explicit by generating critiques, rubrics, or intermediate analyses before predicting a final preference. However, explicit evaluation does not necessarily imply a reliable evaluation process: under outcome-only supervision, a model may reach the correct final preference while producing weak or unsupported intermediate judgments, turning the evaluation into a post-hoc rationalization. We introduce STEP-GRM, a framework that directly supervises the intermediate evaluation process of rubric-based GRMs. In addition to conventional preference supervision, STEP-GRM provides structural guidance for rubric construction and local supervision for criterion-level judgments, encouraging the model to learn not only the correct final preference but also a more reliable process for reaching it. Extensive experiments show that STEP-GRM achieves strong performance on standard reward-modeling benchmarks while improving the consistency and correctness of intermediate evaluations. Moreover, reward signals produced by STEP-GRM lead to better downstream policy optimization, demonstrating that more reliable evaluation processes can translate into practical gains beyond reward-model accuracy.

candidates.title: Breaking the Binary-Lifting Barrier for DNA Minimizer Density: Exact Optimization of a Native 4-ary Order at (w, k) = (12, 5)
candidates.abstract: Minimizer schemes sample at least one $k$-mer from every window of $w$ consecutive $k$-mers via a total order $π$ on $Σ^k$. For DNA ($σ= 4$), state-of-the-art lookup schemes such as GreedyMini and OptMini optimize a binary order ($2^k$ ranks) and lift it to $Σ^k$ by ranking one bit-plane primarily and breaking $2^k$-way ties lexicographically on the other bit-plane. At $(w, k) = (12, 5)$, this projection locks sets of $32$ DNA $5$-mers into contiguous blocks and restricts the active universal hitting set (UHS) prefix to $448$ of $1024$ $5$-mers, giving exact expected DNA density $2246214544 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1307468945$ for OptMini (k5-w12-13.txt) and $2248978620 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1309077849$ for GreedyMini (w12_k5.gm). We bypass binary lifting and optimize directly over native $4$-ary permutations ($|Σ^k| = 1024$) from scratch via: (i) an exact de Bruijn endpoint transfer-matrix dynamic program over $B(4, 4)$ ($256$ states), (ii) a weighted set-cover ratio initializer (SetCover4) producing a compact $U = 314$ UHS prefix, (iii) bitmask-sparse simulated annealing preserving the zero-cost $w$-walk-free tail invariant, and (iv) two-pass $O(N)$ exact best-insertion sweeps with large-neighborhood ruin-and-recreate search. The resulting explicit $4$-ary order achieves exact expected DNA density $2234289615 / 2^{34} \approx 0.130052772292$ (density factor $1.690686$), cutting charged windows by $11924929$ contexts ($-0.530890\%$ relative) below OrensteinLab/Minimizers and $14689005$ ($-0.653141\%$) below w12_k5.gm at $8200$-byte lookup storage ($1280$ bytes bit-packed). Warm-start relaxation stalls at $U = 379$ ($0.1301728789$), whereas native $4$-ary initialization breaks $32/32$ high-bit blocks across all $2+2$ nucleotide partitions.
candidates.comment: 5 pages, 1 table; includes 7 ancillary files in anc/ (explicit 1,024-entry 4-ary minimizer rank tables in .gm and .csv formats, standalone Python 3 standard-library exact verifier, and cold-start C99 optimizer sources)

candidates.title: RetraQ: Manifold-Constrained Critic Guidance for Flow Policies in RL
candidates.abstract: A learned critic can improve a pretrained flow-matching policy by steering sampled actions toward higher predicted value. However, even a critic that fits the behavior data well can provide misleading action gradients. Gradient components pointing away from the data-supported region are weakly constrained by behavior data and can lead guidance to exploit critic extrapolation errors. We introduce RetraQ (Retraction-based Q-guidance), which uses geometry encoded by the pretrained flow to constrain both the direction and the destination of critic guidance. A single velocity evaluation of the frozen flow defines a denoising map. RetraQ filters the critic gradient with the map's Jacobian and applies the map itself to correct the updated action. Our analysis characterizes when these operations approximate tangent filtering and retraction onto the behavior manifold. The same update guides actions at test time and provides targets for policy distillation and online reinforcement learning. In controlled studies, RetraQ improves true return while keeping refined actions close to the data-supported region, and its distillation targets remain more stable than those of raw critic ascent. In offline-to-online training on LIBERO and OGBench, RetraQ achieves higher mean final success than the evaluated critic-guidance baselines. On a real-world plug-insertion task, test-time RetraQ improves the success rate of a behavior-cloned $π_{0.5}$ policy from 55.0% to 76.7%. Online training further increases success to 98.3% in only 30 minutes and 100% within one hour. Project page: https://2027ICLR.github.io/retraq/

candidates.title: Calibrated Reading of Latent Reasoning and Communication
candidates.abstract: Latent reasoning and key-value communication store intermediate information in continuous representations, limiting direct inspection of model behavior. Existing activation readers trade the low cost of task-specific probes against the flexibility of language-model decoders. We propose the Calibrated Latent Reader, CLR, a compact transformer that predicts reasoning outcomes and message content through task-conditioned interactions between states and candidate answers. Source adapters support transfer across models, while conformal calibration provides coverage and false-alarm guarantees under exchangeability. On two CODI models, CLR improves accuracy over MLP and attention probes by 4-18 percentage points for final-answer prediction and reference-value membership. On CODI-GPT-2, it achieves accuracy comparable to a 1.7B LatentQA-based verbalizer using 437-648 times fewer inference FLOPs. On synthetic Qwen3-4B communications, comparing decoded facts with public commitments detects 93.1% of message substitutions at a nominal 5% false-positive rate.

candidates.title: Rethinking Reasoning Effort Training in Large Language Models: On-Policy Distillation or Reinforcement Learning?
candidates.abstract: Large language models have shown strong capabilities on complex tasks, yet how to control their reasoning effort remains a significant challenge for practical deployment. This paper provides a systematic investigation of reasoning-effort training, contrasting reinforcement learning (RL) with on-policy distillation (OPD). We find that compressing reasoning and separating effort tiers are governed by different signals. Length-penalized RL reliably compresses a single policy, reducing thinking on AIME25 by 70\% without accuracy loss, but collapses the tiers when they are trained jointly. Multi-teacher OPD separates them: across 33 benchmarks, low and medium use 58\% and 43\% fewer thinking tokens than high, while high improves on the reference policy by 3.1 points. We trace this difference to the training signal. A sequence-level reward cannot tell tier-specific behavior from shared behavior, whereas OPD supplies a tier-specific target at every visited state, including the decision to stop. Building on this analysis, we show that a single token-level KL anchor on the high tier is sufficient to learn separated tiers within one RL stage, and that natural-language effort instructions make this separation emerge from the start of training, yielding a policy competitive with multi-teacher OPD at matched thinking length. Finally, the separation built by dense targets holds only on the states seen in training: it does not carry over to unseen agentic tasks, where effort acts mainly through the number of interaction turns, whereas the compression induced by sequence-level rewards does.

candidates.title: CoverMem: Coverage-Constrained Visual Memory for Budgeted Embodied Question Answering
candidates.abstract: Episodic-memory embodied question answering enables agents to answer questions based on previously recorded visual observations of the surrounding scenes. However, growing observation histories, varying observation quality across viewpoints, and limited computational resources make it challenging to construct and maintain compact visual memories while retrieving sufficient evidence for question answering. To address these challenges, we introduce CoverMem, which incorporates three key components: (1) a coverage-constrained memory construction method that selects a compact set of informative full frames satisfying object-quality and representative-scene coverage requirements; (2) a coverage-preserving incremental maintenance strategy that locally reselects only the affected frames to satisfy updated coverage requirements as observations arrive; and (3) a budgeted complementary frame selection method that balances question relevance, additional support for question requirements, and redundancy with selected frames within a fixed budget. Experimental results on three benchmarks covering diverse environments and question types demonstrate that CoverMem improves question-answering performance under limited visual budgets.

candidates.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Classifier Chains
candidates.abstract: Multi-label classification continues to be relevant to a variety of modern tasks. Among other challenges, modern data sets are increasingly large with respect to the number of labels, and these labels may be noisy or missing in the training sets. Label-wise scores and ranking-based metrics have been popular, but optimising exact multi-label evaluation (where a predicted set of labels should match the true set exactly) is particularly relevant for many domains, e.g., in medicine; alongside some measure of confidence. This requires an estimation of joint probability across labels (a model of label dependence; conditioned on each input instance). A family of methods known as probabilistic classifier chains provides such inference. However, these existing varieties either do not scale to a large number of labels or do so by approximating joint via marginal distributions in a way that compromises the estimation of uncertainty for exact match accuracy. We overcome this issue by proposing TSCC; leveraging a Monte Carlo Tree Search methodology to enhance chain inference via an efficient balance between the exploration of label space and the exploration of promising label-set predictions. Results are promising both in terms of predictive and computational performance.

candidates.title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models
candidates.abstract: Adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar enables privacy-preserving, all-weather physical scene understanding across darkness, smoke, and walls. However, standard instruction tuning treats continuous radar streams as static text-like tokens, causing near-random global radar-to-text retrieval and severe physical drift under sensor blackouts. Conversely, coupling pairwise contrastive losses (e.g., SigLIP) directly into the shared backbone improves retrieval but injects $O(B^2)$ repulsive gradients that fracture continuous coordinate manifolds ($R^2 < 0$). We present PhysRF-WorldJEPA, a manifold-decoupled Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) that separates continuous electromagnetic state prediction from cross-modal language alignment. An unattenuated 1.0x clock anchor and parallel dual-scale RF encoder feed a lean ~3% LoRA LLM trained with two-step state-space EMA-JEPA (Denoise -> Rollout) and sample-axis Batch-VICReg to predict +3.0 s physical states; a stop-gradient alignment head then maps frozen prompt states onto the text hypersphere with false-negative masking. On a 4,541-window tri-domain suite (77/60.25/60 GHz) against 10 baselines, freezing the physical backbone and training only the decoupled head lifts R->T R@10 from 5.95% to 15.01% and improves MedRank from 107.0 to 60.0 while preserving identical physical readout: 3.37 deg ($R^2=+0.961$) blackout +3.0 s torso tilt, 1.89 m ($R^2=+0.679$; 1.19 m/+0.863 at the RF front-end) cluttered UAV altitude, 2.04 m ($R^2=+0.461$) behind-wall NLOS range, 0.9976 virtual-RIS invariance, and 100% fall recall. Across five 0.5B-1.8B LLM families (15 zero-overhead models), World-JEPA improves retrieval and 75%-drop completion in 10/10 runs and blackout tilt in 4/5 (Span-Euc), 2/5 (Scatter), and 5/5 (per-family best) over SFT.

candidates.title: Duo: Towards Spatiotemporal Action Coordination in Bimanual Policies
candidates.abstract: Bimanual manipulation requires each arm to perform distinct motions while coordinating with the other. Common flow-based robotic policies combine both arms' actions into one token per future timestep, giving attention distinct positions across time but not across arms. We introduce Duo, a simple but effective design that models spatial and temporal dependencies within one shared action head. Specifically, Duo separates both arms into two action tokens per timestep, allowing each arm's motion to interact via cross-arm attention during flow matching. On RoboTwin 2.0, Duo improves the overall success of all four base policies, from 0.45B to 3.62B parameters, with gains of 12.55 and 9.02 percentage points for FLOWER (0.89B) and $π_{0.5}$ (3.62B), respectively. Despite its compact size, FLOWER-Duo achieves the best randomized-generalization, precision, and memory scores on RoboDojo. In real-world tasks, it outperforms $π_{0.5}$ in both success rate and execution speed, while scaling effectively with increasing training data. To provide deeper insight into the design of Duo, we conduct systematic ablations on inter-arm coordination, action grouping, and token granularity, confirming that cross-arm attention drives the improvement while arm-wise interaction offers the best accuracy-compute trade-off.

candidates.title: Ego2Real: Learning Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Visuo-Tactile Demonstrations
candidates.abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from egocentric human demonstrations offers a scalable path toward robot skill acquisition. Vision alone, however, provides limited information about physical contacts and the demonstrator's force intent, leading to ambiguities in interpreting hand-object interactions. Capturing human touch via tactile sensing is therefore crucial for reliable human-to-robot dexterous skill transfer. We present Ego2Real, a framework that leverages egocentric demonstrations and tactile gloves to transfer bimanual dexterous manipulation skills to robotic hands. Ego2Real incorporates tactile supervision at two complementary stages: (1) tactile-guided hand-object interaction reconstruction, which uses measured tactile signals to refine hand poses and contact geometry; and (2) contact-informed reinforcement learning, which translates human contact patterns into robotic contact rewards. By combining refined motion references with physical contact rewards during training, Ego2Real guides anthropomorphic robotic hands to emulate demonstrated contact behaviors while adapting to their own morphology and actuation. Experiments show that incorporating tactile supervision into both reconstruction and policy learning yields higher manipulation success rates, underscoring the importance of enriching egocentric demonstrations with tactile observations to improve their quality and transferability.

candidates.title: ActiveBridge: Scaling Active Prior for Robots through Egocentric Perception-Interaction Modeling
candidates.abstract: Robotics foundation models are now widely used for manipulation, and egocentric videos offer rich data for scaling. However, existing methods overlook the human active priors captured in egocentric videos, which limits performance in unstructured scenes. They act on given observations instead of actively seeking information as humans do. We propose ActiveBridge, a training framework that learns these human active priors and transfers them to robots through world-action modeling. We design a robot that actively controls its viewpoint through head actions to acquire the visual information needed for manipulation using a single head camera, without wrist cameras. During human training, an instruction-conditioned model jointly predicts future egocentric videos and synchronized head-wrist action trajectories, with head actions providing explicit supervision for active perception. Experiments show that ActiveBridge outperforms baselines on active manipulation tasks, while ablations demonstrate the benefit of joint head-wrist action supervision.

candidates.title: MARGIN: A Risk-Aware Agent for Robot Program Refinement
candidates.abstract: Robot-programming agents improve executable control policies through repeated testing and repair, yet binary success saturates while execution risk persists across unseen scenes. We introduce MARGIN, a risk-aware agent that converts successful robot rollouts into actionable evidence for program refinement. Its near-miss margin measures the fraction of the execution budget remaining in the slowest successful development rollout. The agent uses this signal to prioritize fragile programs, guide targeted repairs, and select revisions that preserve development success while increasing execution headroom. An exact safe-racing rule accelerates success-based candidate evaluation. We evaluate MARGIN across LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-90, and Robosuite. In our 80-task LIBERO-Pro reproduction, 78 programs attain perfect development success while accounting for substantial failures on unseen seeds. The near-miss margin predicts held-out failures with an AUC of 0.774, and low-margin programs exhibit 2.97 times higher failure risk. Across two independent evaluation rounds spanning 37 unique LIBERO-Pro tasks, MARGIN reduces executed control steps by 10.7% and 15.0%, with reductions of 18.0-20.0% on LIBERO-90 and Robosuite. Safe racing reduces fixed-sequence candidate-evaluation episodes by 53.5% while retaining identical selections, and paired execution probes improve acceptance decisions by identifying hidden regressions. Together, these results establish near-miss evidence as an effective basis for risk-aware, budget-efficient robot program refinement.

candidates.title: A Fused Gaussian Process Bandit Framework for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization
candidates.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used to maximize expensive black-box functions when direct evaluation is costly. In many real-world applications, the high-fidelity objective can be approximated by a series of lower-fidelity models that provide partial but informative signals at substantially reduced cost. Multi-fidelity BO (MFBO) algorithms aim to strategically combine these information sources to achieve an optimal trade-off between accuracy and evaluation cost. However, existing MFBO methods often oversimplify the complex dependencies between fidelity levels or rely on heuristic acquisition functions that lack theoretical performance guarantees. To address these limitations, we introduce a new formulation of the MFBO problem as a fused Gaussian Process bandit and develop a corresponding Fused Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (FGP-UCB) algorithm. Our approach accurately predicts the high-fidelity function by fusing multi-fidelity observations through an autoregressive Gaussian Process model and explicitly quantifies the uncertainty arising from parameter estimation across fidelity levels. The proposed method also provides theoretical simple-regret guarantees, overcoming a key limitation of existing MFBO algorithms that lack provable performance bounds. Effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated via both theoretical analysis and empirical studies.

candidates.title: From Memory Access to Evidence Sufficiency: Diagnosing and Addressing Demand--Evidence Misalignment
candidates.abstract: Long-term memory retrieval often returns query-relevant records, but relevance does not guarantee sufficient evidence: answering requires a set of records that jointly satisfies a question's factual, relational, temporal, and state constraints. We study this demand--evidence misalignment through MemPath, an interventional framework that diagnoses failures in memory access, demand coverage, and evidence utilization. Guided by this diagnosis, we propose BiDE-Mem, which represents questions as typed demands and uses them to guide retrieval and evidence organization. We formalize demand--evidence support; in the evaluated compact path, it is conveyed through provenance-aware evidence organization and Reader guidance rather than a separate generative four-state verification step. On LoCoMo, BiDE-Mem improves accuracy by 6.23 percentage points over Mnemis; on LongMemEval, it achieves 91.80%, with strong multi-hop and temporal performance. Supplementary Qwen-Reader evaluations place it first among seven systems on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S under two judging protocols. Ablations and evidence-level analyses show that demand representation, retrieval, and evidence presentation each contribute to answer quality.

candidates.title: ExpGuard: Guarding Long-Horizon LLM Agents against Corrupted Experience
candidates.abstract: Long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents distill past trajectories into reusable experiences. Misleading or adversarial guidance in source trajectories can corrupt these experiences, allowing harmful instructions to persist across tasks and influence future agent actions. Assessing the risks of potentially corrupted experiences poses three challenges: (1) modeling provenance and execution dependencies before experience reuse, (2) learning task-conditioned risk from trajectory outcomes, and (3) repairing risky experiences at online inference. To address these challenges, we present ExpGuard, a framework for retrieval-triggered experience risk assessment and online repair. Specifically, to tackle challenge (1), ExpGuard integrates experience semantics with provenance and execution dependencies in a task-conditioned heterogeneous graph to predict attack and task-failure risks before experience reuse. To enable task-conditioned risk supervision and tackle challenge (2), we conduct matched counterfactual replays of each original experience and its minimally neutralized counterpart from the same task and environment checkpoint, deriving separate risk labels from differences in attack success and legitimate task completion. To tackle challenge (3) at inference time, ExpGuard repairs candidate experiences flagged as high-risk by the graph-based predictor at retrieval and re-predicts their risks before they enter the agent's active experience context. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of ExpGuard in identifying risky experiences and defending agents against experience corruption.

candidates.title: KeyMemVLA: Subtask-Guided Key Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Memory-dependent long-horizon manipulation requires vision-language-action (VLA) policies to infer task progress and recall evidence absent from current observations. Under a limited memory budget, the challenge is to retain history that resolves stage ambiguity and supports subsequent decisions. We present KeyMemVLA, a subtask-guided key memory framework based on progress indication and decision-evidence retention. A two-level annotation process selects subtasks satisfying either criterion and labels their final frames as keyframes to supervise online memory writes. A shared vision-language backbone jointly learns subtask, action, and keyframe prediction. At inference, the policy first predicts the current subtask from the instruction, visual context, and memory, then uses this semantic condition to predict actions and future memory-write positions. Actual observations are retained at the selected times during execution. We introduce KMBench to evaluate active memory retention for decisions across subtasks. Evaluations on RMBench-$M(n)$, RoboTwin-MeM, KMBench, and real-world manipulation tasks show higher average success rates than the compared baselines. Ablation studies and representation analysis support the roles of key memory and explicit task-progress semantics. These results highlight the value of coupling sparse key memory with online progress inference for history-dependent control.

candidates.title: Fix How It Acts, Not How It Thinks: Surgical Fine-Tuning of Frontier LLMs
candidates.abstract: Open-weight LLMs are competent software engineers, but they sometimes fail at tasks they are otherwise able to do. Often it is not a failure of reasoning. It is a few small missteps over a long trajectory (repeating a step that has already failed, or declaring the task done while a requirement is still unmet) that make the difference. Correcting this calls for a surgical weight update that steers the model toward the right actions without interfering with its reasoning. Such updates, typically learned with LoRA adapters, are often too small to survive merging into a released checkpoint. In our BF16 release, the median weight change is only 1.5% of a single rounding step, and merging loses roughly two thirds of the update's norm. When the same adapter is merged into the mixed FP8/NVFP4 release of the same model, 93% of the update disappears. Instead of increasing the size of the update, we directly train on the surviving part. We introduce merge-aware fine-tuning. Standard LoRA rounds the merged weights to the storage format only at export, so the loss never sees the rounded weights. We instead round the sum of base weights and adapter update to the release format at every training step, keeping the vendor's quantization scales, and compute the loss on these weights. The forward pass matches the serving engine numerics, and the gradient passes straight through the rounding, so the model we train is the model we ship. The loss optimizes only the model's actions and keeps its reasoning close to the base model. Applied to Nemotron-3.5, the recipe improves agentic coding in both the BF16 and the NVFP4 release, by up to 8.4 points on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and we publicly release both models.
candidates.comment: 30 pages, 4 figures, 9 tables. Models released at https://huggingface.co/abacusai/Smaug-Nemotron-3.5 and https://huggingface.co/abacusai/Smaug-Nemotron-3.5-NVFP4

candidates.title: Integral DeltaNet: Improved Linear Attention with Adaptive Memory Integration
candidates.abstract: Linear attention replaces softmax attention with a linear formulation, enabling linear-time computation with a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing key-value cache. These computational and memory advantages have attracted growing interest in linear attention for long-context language modeling. However, compressing past information into a fixed-size state causes memory collisions that hinder long-context understanding. Although DeltaNet mitigates memory collisions through delta-rule updates and Gated DeltaNet extends this approach with gating, these mechanisms may also discard information relevant to future predictions. To address this limitation, we introduce Integral DeltaNet, which maintains two complementary recurrent states: a fast-updating delta state that captures current key-value associations and an integral state that preserves a weighted history of the delta state. At readout, the model adaptively combines these states to access information across different timescales. We further derive a chunkwise parallel formulation that enables hardware-efficient training. We evaluate Integral DeltaNet using 340M and 1.3B parameter models trained from scratch on 15B and 100B FineWeb-Edu tokens, respectively. Comparisons with strong recurrent baselines show improved overall performance in language modeling, commonsense reasoning, real-world and synthetic retrieval, long-context understanding, and length extrapolation. We also compare training throughput and activation memory, as well as decoding latency and memory.

candidates.title: More Powerful, Less Verifiable? Mitigating Hard-to-Verify Hallucinations in MLLM's Reinforcement Learning
candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) strengthens model capabilities through feedback from humans and environments. However, emerging evidence suggests that reward optimization can produce outputs whose errors are harder for humans to detect. To address this issue, we construct ITHV (the Image-Text Hallucination Verifiability Dataset), comprising 2,728 visually grounded instances that distinguish between obvious hallucinations, which humans readily detect, and elusive hallucinations, which humans struggle to identify. We then propose DAPO-V, an extension of DAPO that maximizes correctness subject to a budget on verifiability-aware risk. Specifically, DAPO-V combines a verifiability-aware reward with adaptive dual control, where larger penalties are assigned to incorrect responses on questions with lower human verification accuracy. An adaptive multiplier further adjusts the penalty strength according to risk-budget violations. Across three MLLM base models, DAPO-V improves overall accuracy while substantially improving accuracy on elusive hallucination questions by 5.78--9.72 percentage points over accuracy-only DAPO. We further test DAPO-V with a blinded human study, which shows that hallucinations are more readily detected in DAPO-V than those of the base model.

candidates.title: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
candidates.abstract: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies Effect targets. A shared generation expert learns to jointly predict Effect and an executable action chunk through flow matching, and reuses the sampled pair to generate future video on demand. This allows the controller to execute actions without waiting for video synthesis. We train on more than 20,000 hours of heterogeneous embodied data, excluding unused chain-of-thought data, and accommodate dataset-specific joint, end-effector, and hand-pose representations. Our evaluation uses the Small (8B) configuration on all five benchmarks and additionally evaluates the Large (26B) configuration on RoboDojo. Experiments examine closed-loop manipulation across complementary benchmarks, and comparisons across multiple baseline policies show consistent improvements from Action Grounding.

candidates.title: From Rule-based to Agentic: LLM Agent based Real-time Control of Urban Drainage Systems for Flooding and Sewer Overflow Mitigation
candidates.abstract: Real-time control (RTC) for urban drainage systems (UDS) remains hampered by sparse in-network sensing. While heterogeneous multi-modal meteorological early warnings often contain decision-critical information for UDS RTC, none of the existing approaches can exploit such externally-sourced information within the control workflow. Here we introduce AgenticAI-Control, an agentic artificial intelligence framework able to assimilate multi-source meteorological early warnings in RTC. Two coupled large language model agents are integrated to generate control strategies by retrieving meteorological early-warnings and fusing them with domain engineering expertise. Validated via simulation studies of a combined sewer catchment in eastern China across 10 real-world rainfall events, the AgenticAI-Control achieved 69.1-90.6% reduction in aggregated flood and overflow volumes compared to the rule-based baseline control. Rigorously standardized prompt engineering and modular workflow constraints substantially compress performance disparities among four distinct LLMs. Our work establishes AgenticAI as a viable tool to unify multi-source meteorological monitoring and practitioner domain knowledge, surmounting longstanding monitoring limitations of UDS RTC and delivering cost-efficient, robust intelligent control solutions for sensor-sparse sewer infrastructures.

candidates.title: Spec-CoFrGeNet: Reparametrizing Continued Fraction Networks for Stable and Accurate Training
candidates.abstract: Continued fractions have been shown to be a function class capable of constructing expressive yet parameter-efficient neural networks. These neural networks are not only effective for supervised learning, but also for training LLMs. However, the rational form of this function class introduces poles when the denominator approaches zero, which prior work has avoided by enforcing a small positive (non-smooth) lower bound. We show that performance and training stability can be highly sensitive to the choice of this lower bound. In this work, we introduce a novel transformation of the partial denominators, inspired by its connection to the Green's function in physics, that mitigates the above issue elegantly by constraining the spectra of the constructed tridiagonal Hamiltonian. Our approach further eliminates the need for incremental training used by previous works for stability, thus avoiding involved modifications to standard pre-training procedures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our reparameterization by replacing FFNs with a previously proposed continued fraction architecture for both language and image generative modeling. Across diverse models, such as GPT-2 XL, (nano) Llama-MoE, and Granite, we show that our proposed method achieves performance comparable to the original (FFN-based) architectures while maintaining ~30%-50% parameter savings as before, and in most cases even outperforms the more complicated incremental training baseline. We further demonstrate, for the first time for continued fraction networks, that their effectiveness also carries over to image generative modeling, that utilize diffusion objectives. On a state-of-the-art Diffusion Transformer, we show that our approach again achieves performance comparable to the original FFN-based models with ~30% parameter savings and significantly outperforms the previous incremental training approach.

candidates.title: FlashQLA: Efficient Context Parallelism for Gated DeltaNet
candidates.abstract: Gated DeltaNet (GDN) achieves linear computational complexity through recurrent state updates, but sequential dependencies between chunks limit parallelism, particularly for long-context workloads with small batch sizes or limited head-level parallelism per GPU. We present FlashQLA, a context-parallel execution framework for GDN that exposes additional sequence-level parallelism while reducing boundary-state preprocessing overhead. FlashQLA reduces boundary-state preprocessing overhead through decay-aware preparation and extends sequence parallelism across GPUs with Dual CP, which shares summary computation across parallelism levels. Workload-adaptive Auto CP and CP-aware kernel co-design further improve execution efficiency. FlashQLA achieves $1.7\times$-$3.1\times$ forward speedup and up to $4.4\times$ backward speedup over Flash Linear Attention (FLA) on a single GPU. On eight GPUs with context lengths up to 1M tokens, Dual CP achieves up to $4.8\times$ forward speedup and $4.4\times$ speedup for combined forward and backward execution over FLA KCP.

candidates.title: Online Environment Repair for Coding Agents
candidates.abstract: Programmatic verifiers provide scalable reward signals for training coding agents with reinforcement learning, yet subtle harness defects and incomplete unit tests allow policies to earn full credit without solving the intended task. Existing training-time defenses intervene either by penalizing suspicious outputs or by filtering flagged tasks and rollouts. However, output penalties leave the underlying verifier exploitable, driving policies to disguise shortcuts under reasoning monitors or zeroing out valid solutions under detector false positives, whereas task and rollout filtering discards or mutes the hardest problems where shortcuts emerge earliest. Pre-training verifier hardening repairs the environment directly, but misses vulnerability classes that surface only as the policy improves during reinforcement learning. In this paper, we propose online environment repair, which leaves triggering rollout rewards unchanged to remove hiding incentives and asynchronously patches exploited environments during training. Candidate repairs triggered by execution invariants or differential fuzzing are deployed only after passing three automated validation gates that block the exploit while preserving valid solutions, canceling detector false positives and enabling structural propagation across repositories without scaffold labels or reference solutions. Across 20 controlled GRPO experiments on heterogeneous software-engineering repositories, online environment repair reduces cumulative reward hacking from 36.9% to 0.06% and improves held-out Pass@8 from 21.7% to 46.7%, consistently outperforming reward-penalty, rollout-filtering, and static-hardening baselines while eliminating zero-shot exploitation on unseen loophole classes.

candidates.title: Scale-Robust and Global-Aware Representation Learning for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
candidates.abstract: Multivariate time series anomaly detection (MTSAD) is an essential task for identifying abnormal system behaviors and supporting reliable operations across diverse real-world applications.
